- **When it applies:** The `{{` list, the palette list and short-word expansion read aliases and snippets when syki::sok starts, so restart it after you edit them. Running `{{ @alias ... }}` and the command bar's drop-down list use the new file without a restart (the agent is looked up when the task runs, and the bar reads the file each time it opens).
- **Command bar:** Command snippets that need no placeholder, in the version for your OS, are also offered in the drop-down list of the command bar.

---

### Delegate · Hand work to an agent ({{ }})

**In one line:** Write `{{ instruction }}` in a note and press Ctrl + Enter. An external agent CLI works in the background, and the whole `{{ }}` is replaced by the result. Name an agent, as in `{{ @claude instruction }}`, and the result goes below your line instead. Agent CLI needed separately

This notation is called a **slot**. To let syki::sok choose the AI, an agent or a command for a plain line, see Delegate · Auto Selector.

A slot while it runs: `{{ }}` becomes a "running" placeholder and the status bar shows a task badge

1. **Running placeholder** It stands in for the slot while the agent works, and the result replaces it (its text is Japanese in both UI languages)
2. **Task badge** The number of running agent tasks. Click it, or press Alt + T, to open the task panel

Write (Ask AI)

- Answers in seconds
- The answer goes in below your text

Delegate (agent)

- Spends minutes on web research or file work
- You can keep editing the note the whole time

Learn `{{ }}` and nothing else

The other notations below are all variations on it. When in doubt, write plain language inside `{{ }}` and it will work.

### How to run one

1. **Type `{{`**A **quick selector** opens just below the caret and lists the notations you can use, then ready-made task snippets
2. **Choose a notation**Move with ↑ ↓ and confirm with Tab or Enter. 1–9 picks an entry at once. Esc closes it
3. **Write the instruction**`{{ code:` … `}}` is inserted, and the caret lands where the instruction goes
4. **Press Ctrl + Enter to run**macOS: Cmd + Enter. You can also click the small **Run** button (it carries a play icon)

```
{{ code: write a Go function that loads this project's config file }}

[? What is Go's release cadence in 2025, and what is the current stable version? ]
```

Limits and details (the run key and input correction)

- **Which one runs:** A slot or task under the caret runs. On a plain line, the Auto selector takes over (it is on by default). When the Auto selector is off, or the line is blank, Ctrl + Enter uses the older rule: it runs the next slot after the caret, and if there is none, the first slot in the note. Inside a code block it does nothing.
- **When none is found:** The status bar shows "No slot found to run (place the cursor inside a {{ }}-style block)." for a few seconds. This appears only when the older rule applies and the note has no slot at all. Your note is not changed.
- **If it is already running:** The status bar shows "This slot is already running."
- **Run button:** A small button with a play icon. It appears next to a complete block that is not running yet, while the caret is inside it (hover text: "Run this slot (Ctrl+Enter)"; on macOS, Cmd+Enter). It also appears at the right end of a task line (`[[ @llm ... ]]`, `[[ $ ... ]]`, `{{ @agent ... }}`) that is not running. Clicking it does the same as pressing Ctrl + Enter.
- **Quick selector:** It also disappears on its own as soon as you keep typing normal words.
- **Japanese input:** If a Japanese IME turns your brackets into full-width characters (`｛｛`, `【？`), they are converted back to half-width automatically.
- **No accidental runs:** Delimiters inside fenced code blocks, inline code, Markdown links and bare URLs are never treated as slots, so a `{{ }}` in a code sample does not fire.

### The default notations

| Notation | Profile | Default agent | What it is for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `{{ ... }}` | code | claude-code | Code generation. Returns a runnable code block with no preamble. |
| `[? ... ]` | research | claude-code | Research. Searches the web and answers concisely with figures and primary-source URLs. |
| `【? ... 】` | writing | hermes | Writing. Stays fully local — no outbound calls — and reshapes the text into clear bullets. |
| `[! ... !]` | adversarial | claude-code | Adversarial review. Names three risks, vulnerabilities, or bottlenecks instead of agreeing with you. |
| `[>> ... ]` | deep-research-and-code (recipe) | default agent | Multi-step run: research → risk critique → implementation, in order. |

- Each notation carries its own agent and its own standing instruction (system instruction), so the same sentence comes back in a different shape depending on which one you use.
- Any slot can start with a role name (for example `{{ research: something to look up }}`). This name becomes the label for that task in the task panel.
- If your project has `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, writing `{{ @skill-name: instruction }}` passes that file's contents to the agent as extra instructions. If it cannot be found, the slot is replaced by an error. A name that is an agent's key or alias is an agent call instead (next item).
- **Naming an agent:** `{{ @claude-code instruction }}` hands the instruction to that agent directly. The name is a key under `agents` in agents.yaml, or one of its `aliases` (not case-sensitive). By default `claude` and `cc` mean claude-code, and `antigravity` and `gemini` mean agy. Unlike the notations above, your line stays and the result goes below it, and the notation's standing instruction (code blocks only) is not applied. Details: Auto Selector.

### While it runs, and the task panel (Alt+T)

The moment a slot starts, it turns into `{{ ⟳ 実行中... }}` in place. A task in the new notations keeps its line and gets a one-line marker below it instead. The agent runs in the background, so you can edit elsewhere in the note, or start several slots at once.

Alt + T: the task panel with two running agent tasks (some texts, such as the elapsed seconds and the clear button, are Japanese even in the English UI)

1. **Task badge** In the status bar. Click it, or press Alt + T, to open the panel
2. **Panel title** The number of active tasks. The clear button empties the history
3. **A running task** Agent name, instruction, elapsed time and a Cancel button
4. **Live output** The agent's latest output (Hover Peek), updated while it runs

- **Task panel:** Press Alt + T (macOS: Option + T), or click the running-task indicator in the status bar. It lists the running tasks and a short history, including AI requests (Ask AI and the Auto selector) and commands. A finished agent task has a **Lessons** button that turns a run that went wrong into a rule for next time (see Lessons).
- **Progress (Hover Peek):** Each task card shows the agent's latest output line, refreshed every second, so you can tell whether it is stuck or moving.
- **Where the answer goes:** Into the note the slot was in, even if you have switched to another note or closed the second pane meanwhile; the note you are looking at is not touched. With several slots running in one note, each answer replaces its own slot, in whatever order the answers come.
- **Cancel:** The card's Cancel button ends the process, and the slot goes back to your original instruction, in the note it was started in even if another note is open now. For a task in the new notations, the marker line under it disappears. If the running mark in the note was edited away, the note is left alone and the status bar says so and shows the instruction.
- **Timeout:** 180 seconds by default. After that the slot is replaced by a timeout message. You can set 10–600 seconds under Settings → Agent, in the "Agents (Request)" section. But if an `agents.yaml` already exists (even one created by "Open agents.yaml"), the file's value wins.

Results are merged only after you have **stopped typing for about half a second**, so an agent finishing mid-sentence never moves your caret out from under you.

### Getting the result, and undoing it

Ghost Diff: the rows a result was inserted into, about 0.3 seconds later

1. **Amber band with a line on its left edge** It covers just the rows the agent result went into. It disappears after the time you set
2. **Inserted text** The agent's result, in place of the slot. Press Esc within the highlight time to restore the original slot

- **Ghost Diff (the amber band):** Right after a result is inserted, the rows it went into get a soft amber wash and a 3 px amber line on their left edge. Nothing else in the note is marked. The band follows the scroll.
- **How long it shows:** Set it with "Change highlight duration (ms) (Ghost Diff)" under Settings → Agent (default 4000 ms, 1000–10000). The band disappears when the time is up, or at once if you edit, undo or replace the marked text or switch to another note. Typing elsewhere leaves it, and it moves with its text; results that arrive one after another each keep their own band.
- **Undo:** During that time (the set time plus 1 second), press Esc and **that slot alone** reverts to your original instruction. Ctrl + Z undoes the last slot run the same way.
- **Inline slots stay inline:** If the slot had other text on its line, line breaks are removed from the result so it stays on one line.
- **Other results:** A result written below a task line, and the answers to Ask AI, the Auto selector, rewrite and proofreading, get the same amber band. The Esc revert belongs only to slots that are replaced by their result; undo the others with Ctrl + Z.

### Lessons · Keep a Rule From a Failed Run

**In one line:** When a delegated agent task fails, or comes back with something you did not want, keep a short rule from that run. From then on syki::sok puts the rule in front of that agent's instruction every time, so it is less likely to make the same mistake again. Nothing is automatic: no rule is written, and nothing is sent to a model, until you press the buttons. LLM setup needed
Alt + T: a failed task with the Lessons button, and a finished task that ran with two saved lessons

1. **Lessons button** On the card of a finished agent task, failed or completed. It opens the dialog below
2. **Lessons applied** On a task that ran with saved rules: how many were put in front of its instruction

The Lessons dialog with two proposed rules, the first one edited a little

1. **Agent** Whose rules these are: the agent's key in agents.yaml. Under it the dialog shows the start of the task
2. **Who proposed** The model that read the record of the run and made the suggestions
3. **A proposed rule** A tick box and one line you can edit. Change the words, or untick a rule you do not want
4. **Save** Adds the ticked rules to the agent's lessons file. Nothing is written before this

1. **Run a delegated task and let it finish**For example `{{ @claude ... }}` with Ctrl + Enter. A run that failed is the usual case, but a run that finished with a result you did not want works too
2. **Open the task panel and press Lessons**Alt + T (macOS: Option + T). The button is on the card of a finished agent task. A task that is still running or was canceled, a recipe, and the cards of AI requests and commands have none
3. **Look at what would be sent**The dialog names the agent and shows the start of the task. It says how many characters of the instruction, of the end of the agent's output and of the error message would go, how many secrets (keys, tokens, passwords) are blanked out, and where it goes. Nothing has been sent yet. You can write what went wrong in the box; that is sent too
4. **Press Create a proposal**Ctrl + Enter does the same (macOS: Cmd + Enter). For a model that is not on this PC, tick the box that names the host first. Esc cancels while the model works
5. **Read, edit and save**The model proposes one or two rules. Edit the words, untick any you do not want, and press **Save**; the status bar says "Lessons saved: claude-code (2)". If it finds nothing worth keeping, the dialog says so: write what went wrong and press **Ask again**, or close it

If no text AI model is set up, the dialog says so and its **Set up** button opens the model settings (Settings → AI Models).

**What is sent, and where**

- **Only after you press Create a proposal.** Opening the dialog sends nothing. What goes is a cut-down record of that one run, not your note: the start of the instruction (up to 1,500 characters), the end of the agent's output (up to 4,000), the error message (up to 800) and what you typed in the box (up to 500). A key, token or password found in them is blanked out first.
- **To your text AI model.** It is the model of Settings → AI Models that the Ask AI bar uses. A model on this PC is not asked about. Any other model, a cloud service or a machine on your local network, is named in the dialog with a box you tick once for that host; it joins the same list of allowed hosts as the Ask AI bar and Deep search. syki::sok checks the permission again before it sends.

**Where the rules are kept**

One plain Markdown file per agent, `lessons/<agent>.md`, in the folder that holds `config.json` (Windows: `%APPDATA%\syki-sok\`; macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/syki-sok/`; About syki::sok shows the exact folder). The agent is its key in agents.yaml, and an alias counts as the key, so `@cc` and `@claude` share the file of claude-code. The command palette entry **Open the lessons file** opens it as an ordinary tab (it asks which agent when several have one). A rule is a line that starts with `-`:

```
# Lessons for claude-code
<!-- syki lessons: one rule per "- " line. Edit or delete freely; other lines are ignored. -->
- Run the tests with `pytest -p no:cacheprovider`; the default cache folder is read-only on this machine. <!-- 2026-10-04 -->
- Do not include ADF.h: the build fails on this machine. <!-- 2026-10-04 -->
```

The date at the end is for you; the agent is not given it. Anything that is not a `-` line is ignored. Edit, reorder or delete lines whenever you like, or delete the file to take every rule away. The file is read again at each run, so nothing needs a restart.

**What the agent is told**

Each time that agent runs a delegated task (`{{ @agent ... }}`, or the default agent of a plain `{{ ... }}` and of what Ctrl + Enter hands over), syki::sok puts the newest rules, the last lines of the file, in front of your instruction under the heading "Lessons from earlier runs on this machine (written or approved by the user; follow them):". The card of that task then says, for example, "2 lessons applied".

Limits and details (how many rules, which tasks, a file that is full, macOS)

- **How many are used:** at most the newest 30 rules and 4,000 characters in all. Older ones are left out, and the card says "N not applied (too many)". Delete rules you no longer need.
- **Which tasks:** single delegated tasks only. Recipes (`[>> ... ]`), `[[ @llm ]]` and `[[ $ ]]` tasks, and Ask AI get no lessons. An agent whose definition never passes `{instruction}` (`append_instruction: false` and no `{instruction}` in its arguments) cannot receive them.
- **How long the button is there:** the task panel keeps the last 10 finished tasks, shows the newest 5, and forgets them when syki::sok closes, so press **Lessons** soon after the run. A run that never started (its agent is switched off or its program was not found) has no button.
- **What the model is asked for:** 0 to 2 one-sentence rules that name the file, command or setting behind this failure on this machine, written in the language of the interface. The record is handed over as data: instructions inside it are not followed. A run that shows nothing worth remembering gets no rules.
- **What a rule may be:** one line of up to 300 characters. syki::sok refuses a rule that contains `<!--` or `-->` (the dialog says so beside it), looks like it holds a key, token or password, or tries to rewrite the agent's instructions (for example "ignore the previous instructions", or the words "system prompt"). A rule that is already in the file is not added twice. A save adds at most 5 rules, and a file holds at most 200: past that the dialog asks you to delete some in the file.
- **Edited by hand:** a line longer than 300 characters, or with a comment mark inside, is not a rule and is ignored. Only the last 64 KB of a file is read.
- **Cost:** nothing until an agent runs: a file that does not exist costs a single check. Each rule used adds its text to every run of that agent, so keep the list short.
- **macOS:** the code is the same, but it has not yet been verified on a real Mac. The dialog has also not been checked with a screen reader, or with a Japanese IME in the box for what went wrong.

**Switch it off for one agent**

Add `lessons: false` to the agent in `agents.yaml`. The rules stay in their file, but that agent is not told them. syki::sok only reads agents.yaml and never rewrites it. For a built-in agent such as claude-code that one line is enough: whatever the entry leaves out (the command, its arguments, its aliases) stays as built in. An entry that has its own `command` is used exactly as written.

```
agents:
  claude-code:
    lessons: false
```

**Reading them from a script, and why nothing writes them**

`syki lessons list [--agent <key>]` and the JSON-RPC method `lessons.list` list the files: for each agent how many rules it holds, how many its next run is given and whether it is switched off (see Headless CLI Commands). They only read. There is deliberately no command or method that adds, changes or removes a rule. The rules are put in front of an agent's instruction, so a way to write them would let an agent rewrite its own future instructions with nobody approving it. A rule enters the file through the dialog above, or by you editing the file.

What to expect

A lesson keeps the same mistake from repeating; it does not promise a better result. A small local model can write vague or overlapping rules, so read and edit them before you save, and delete a rule that stops being true. The idea comes from the GEPA paper on reflective prompt evolution (arXiv 2507.19457), which reports gains from letting a model reflect on its failures in words. syki::sok takes only that one step (the model reflects, you approve, the rule is kept) and none of the automatic optimization.

### Approval gates in recipes

A recipe such as `[>> ... ]` runs several steps in order. To put a human check before a risky step, set `requires_approval_step` on the recipe. The run pauses after that step, and a line like this is inserted into the note (the inserted text is Japanese in both UI languages):

```
- [ ] 次のステップ（実装コードを生成する）を実行する // approve
```

1. **Review what you have so far**Change `[ ]` to `[x]`
2. **Press Ctrl + Enter**The run continues. If you leave the box unchecked, it stays stopped there

When the last step finishes, its output replaces the recipe line (or the checked gate line). Earlier steps' output stays where the run paused.

### Agent CLIs are installed separately

syki::sok does not bundle any agent. Install the commands you intend to use — `claude`, `codex`, `ollama`, `agy` — and make sure they are on your PATH.

If the program an agent needs cannot be found in PATH, syki::sok says so **before it starts anything**, for example `Agent "hermes" needs "ollama", which was not found in PATH. Install it or choose another agent in agents.yaml.` The note is left exactly as it was: no running placeholder, no marker, no error text written into the slot. In the list that opens when you type `{{`, a row whose agent's program is not found carries a small "not found" tag. Only the program is checked, not the model or the login it may need (`ollama run` may start downloading a model by itself).

An agent that acts without asking is confirmed first

Before an agent runs, syki::sok looks at its definition in `agents.yaml`. If it carries a flag that skips the agent's own permission prompts (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, `--yolo`, `--full-auto`, `--auto-approve`), or it is a shell that would run your instruction as a command (see `append_instruction` below), a dialog names the agent, the flag, what it does and the command line. **Run** starts the agent, and syki::sok does not ask again for that agent until its command line changes. **Cancel** (it has the focus; Esc does the same) runs nothing and leaves the note exactly as it was.

This covers every way an agent starts: `{{ }}` slots, `{{ @agent }}` tasks, recipes and the Auto Selector. Settings → Agent also warns when the selected agent is set up this way. The check is a list of known flags, not a sandbox: an agent can still do whatever its CLI allows. None of the built-in agents carries such a flag.

Limits and details (error display, working directory and .env)

When an agent cannot be started (a program that is not in PATH is caught before this, see above), the slot is replaced by an error like the one below (the inserted text is Japanese in both UI languages). Fix the cause, put the caret back in that slot and press Ctrl + Enter to run it again.

```
{{ ⚠ エラー: エージェント起動失敗: ... (再試行: Ctrl+Enter) }}
```

- **Working directory:** The **project root**, found by walking up from the note until a folder that contains `.syki/`, `.syki/`, `agents.yaml` (or `agents.yml` / `agents.json`), `AGENTS.md`, `skills/` or `.git/`. If none is found, it is the note's own folder.
- **.env:** If the project root has a `.env` file, its variables are passed to the agent as environment variables (only that file is read).
- **Tasks with a result below:** The error is one line inside the result block, such as `[claude-code error: ...]`. Fix the cause and press Ctrl + Enter on the task line to run it again.

### Customizing it in agents.yaml

Every notation, agent, alias, recipe and snippet can be changed or added in `agents.yaml`.

1. **Click "Open agents.yaml"**It is in Settings → Agent, in the "Agents (Request)" section. If the file does not exist, a commented template is created and opened
2. **Edit notations, agents, aliases, recipes and snippets**Save the file as UTF-8 without a BOM
3. **It takes effect on the next slot run**If the file has a syntax error, syki::sok silently falls back to the defaults. If you changed notations (`slot_profiles` / `recipes`), aliases or snippets, restart syki::sok so the `{{` list, the palette list and short-word expansion see them (running a `{{ @alias }}` task and the command bar list already use the new file)

The first file found, from the top, is used (`.yaml`, `.yml`, `.md` and `.json` are all accepted):

1. `<scraps folder>/.syki-sok/agents.yaml` (per-project settings)
2. `%APPDATA%\syki-sok\agents.yaml` (macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/syki-sok/agents.yaml`)

The built-in agents changed after v1.8.0, and your agents.yaml is not rewritten

The built-in definitions (and the template that "Open agents.yaml" writes) are now:

- **claude-code:** `claude -p "対象ノート: {file}\n指示: {instruction}"`. Before: `--file {file} --prompt {instruction}`; Claude Code has no `--prompt` option and its `--file` expects `file_id:path`, so the instruction did not reach it.
- **codex:** `codex exec {instruction}`. Before: `--execute --file {file}`, options Codex CLI does not have.
- **agy:** `agy -p "対象ノート: {file}\n指示: {instruction}"`, without `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. agy may now stop when it needs a permission that print mode cannot ask for. If you want the old behaviour, add the flag back to `args` in agents.yaml; syki::sok then asks you once before it runs.

These command lines were not run on the maintainer's machine: `codex exec` and `agy -p` are what those CLIs list in their `--help`, and Claude Code is not installed there. Check each CLI's `--help`. Codex may refuse to work outside a Git repository; its `--help` lists `--skip-git-repo-check` for that.

An agents.yaml you already have is used as it is. If it still holds one of the old definitions (the template written by earlier versions does), Settings → Agent shows **Agent definitions to review**, and the status bar says so once a few seconds after start-up. **Copy the new definition** copies a replacement entry (your key, description and aliases are kept): open agents.yaml and paste it over the old entry, or delete the entry to use the built-in one. **Hide until this list changes** hides the box. The same box warns about a shell agent that would run your instruction as a command.

Switching an agent off (enabled: false, disabled_agents)

Deleting a built-in agent (`claude-code`, `hermes`, `codex`, `agy`) from agents.yaml does nothing: it is added back the next time the file is read. To take one out for good, **switch it off**. There are two spellings; use either or both (they are added together):

```
disabled_agents: [agy, hermes]   # top level: list the keys

agents:
  codex:
    enabled: false               # or on the agent itself
```

- **Never chosen:** A disabled agent is not listed in Settings → Agent, has no row in the list that opens when you type `{{` (a notation whose agent is disabled has no row either), is never picked by the Auto selector or a snippet, and cannot be the default agent.
- **Its aliases go with it:** Switching `agy` off frees `gemini` and `antigravity`.
- **Naming it anyway:** A note that says `{{ @agy ... }}` shows `Agent "agy" is disabled in agents.yaml (enabled: false)`. Nothing runs, the note is left as it was, and no other agent takes over. The same goes for a notation in `slot_profiles` whose `agent` is disabled.
- **The default agent:** If `default_agent` names a disabled agent, the first enabled one is used instead (in the order claude-code, hermes, codex, agy, then the others by name). agents.yaml itself is not changed, and **Agent definitions to review** in Settings → Agent tells you.
- **Everything switched off:** Running then says `No agent is enabled: every agent is disabled in agents.yaml (enabled: false)`, and the Agent list in Settings is grayed out.

Example and writing rules

```
version: 2
default_agent: claude-code
timeout_seconds: 180
hover_peek_enabled: true
ghost_diff_duration_ms: 4000

# 1. The CLIs to call. {instruction} becomes your prompt, {file} the note's absolute path.
agents:
  claude-code:
    command: "claude"
    args: ["-p", "Note: {file}\nInstruction: {instruction}"]
    description: "Claude Code"
  my-agent:
    command: "my-cli"
    args: ["--prompt", "{instruction}"]
    description: "Our in-house agent"
    aliases: ["mine"]   # {{ @mine ... }} calls my-agent

# 2. Notation-to-agent mapping. Only what you list here stays active.
slot_profiles:
  - trigger_open: "{{"
    trigger_close: "}}"
    name: "code"
    agent: "claude-code"
    system_instruction: "Skip any preamble and output only a runnable code block."

  - trigger_open: "<<"
    trigger_close: ">>"
    name: "review"
    agent: "my-agent"
    system_instruction: "Review the changes and report your findings as bullet points."

# 3. Recipes run several steps in sequence.
recipes:
  - trigger_open: "[>>"
    trigger_close: "]"
    name: "deep-research-and-code"
    description: "Research -> risk critique -> implementation"
    steps:
      - "Research the current official specification and best practices"
      - "Point out migration risks and breaking changes"
      - "Generate the implementation based on the above"
    requires_approval_step: 2
    self_refine: true
```

- **Placeholders:** `{instruction}` is replaced by what you wrote in the slot, `{file}` by the current note's absolute path. If you never mention `{instruction}`, it is appended as the final argument; write `append_instruction: false` in an agent that should not get it (one that works from `{file}` alone).
- **Shells:** for a shell (`powershell`, `pwsh`, `cmd`, `sh`, `bash`, `zsh`, or an argument `-Command`, `/c`, `-c`) the appended instruction would run as a command. Settings → Agent warns about such a definition, and syki::sok asks before it runs, until you add `append_instruction: false` or place `{instruction}` yourself.
- **Choosing delimiters:** pick `trigger_open` / `trigger_close` pairs that do not collide with ordinary Markdown syntax (`#`, `*`, `-`, and so on).
- **How overriding works:** writing `slot_profiles` or `recipes` **replaces** the defaults, so copy over any of the four built-in notations you still want. `agents` behaves differently: built-in agents you don't override are kept, with today's built-in definition, and an agent you write is used exactly as written. To take a built-in agent out for good, switch it off (see "Switching an agent off" just above); deleting it changes nothing.
- **self_refine:** set it to `true` and the recipe's first step runs a draft → self-critique → revise loop (up to two passes) before moving on.
- **aliases and snippets:** `aliases` gives an agent extra names for `{{ @name ... }}`, and `snippets` adds your own ready-made tasks. Both are described under Auto Selector.
- **lessons:** `lessons: false` on an agent keeps the rules you saved with the Lessons button from being put in front of its instruction (see Lessons). syki::sok only reads it and never writes it.
- Save the file as UTF-8 without a BOM.

---

### Suggest · Quick Actions (Ctrl+J)

**In one line:** The "I don't know what to do next" button. syki::sok reads what you are writing and proposes **up to three next steps** as cards. Ctrl + J Works with built-in rules
Ctrl + J: the Quick Actions panel with three suggestions (Delegate, Run, Write)

1. **Panel header** Key hints: Ctrl+1..3 runs a suggestion at once, Ctrl+Tab moves the highlight, Enter confirms and Esc closes
2. **Delegate** Hands the work to an agent that runs in the background
3. **Run** Executes a command and inserts its output
4. **Write** The built-in AI writes text and inserts it

The cards are chosen to be unlike each other in kind. Picking one takes you straight to that verb's entry point.

Delegate

- Inserts a `{{ … }}` or `[? … ]` slot and hands it to an agent

Run

- Runs a shell command such as `git status`

Write

- Has the AI draft text
- Appears only when a non-Jev external model is configured (an OpenRouter chat model or your own `/predict` server)

With the built-in local rules (the default), you get Delegate and Run cards, typically in the order Delegate, Run, Delegate.

**When Jev is set up:** the cards are the same built-in ones, and Jev picks the ones that fit your note and ranks them first. Jev never writes text. How to set it up and where the data goes is under "data that is sent", below.

Ctrl1–3Run a card directlymacOS: Cmd + 1–3. Alt + 1–3 also work
CtrlTabMove the selectionCtrl + Shift + Tab goes back. It is the Ctrl key on macOS too
EnterRun the selected cardPress it after moving the selection with Ctrl + Tab
EscCloseCloses the panel

Safety check before running

Cards that run a shell command always go through a safety check first. If it finds a destructive command such as `rm`, `dd` or `mkfs`, a write into a protected system directory, or a fork bomb, the card is not run and the reason is shown. It guards against known dangerous patterns, so read the command yourself before you accept it.

Limits and details (panel behavior, auto-suggest, badge)

- **Hint line:** While the panel is open it shows "Ctrl+1..3 Run now / Ctrl+Tab Move → Enter Confirm / Esc Close".
- **A bare Enter:** If you press Enter without first moving the selection with Ctrl + Tab, it is just a newline. No card runs, and the panel closes.
- **It stays out of your typing:** Bare digits, a bare Tab and Ctrl + Enter (the Auto selector's key, which also runs slots) are never taken by the panel.
- **Where the result goes:** Right below the line with the caret, in the note where you asked. If you open another note before the result arrives, it is not inserted (the panel says so): press Ctrl + J again where you want it.
- **Auto-suggest:** Besides Ctrl + J, the panel can appear on its own after a typing pause (on by default). To stop that, choose "Manual trigger only (suppress auto-popup, press Ctrl+J)" under Settings → Agent, in the "Suggestions (Quick Actions)" section. The delay before it appears is set there too.
- **Changing the key:** The shortcut itself can be reassigned under Settings → Shortcuts.
- **Status bar switches:** Click **AI** in the status bar. **Suggestions** turns the feature on or off, and **Only when I press Ctrl+J** (your configured key; Cmd+J on macOS) below it switches between On and Manual. They mirror the two checkboxes under Settings → Agent → Suggestions (Quick Actions). While Suggestions are off, Ctrl + J does nothing.
- **Commands with no output:** If a Run card (an `sh` card) command succeeds but prints nothing, `> (出力なし)` is inserted so you can tell it ran. This applies to Quick Actions only (the command bar shows "(no output)" in its result tab). The inserted text is Japanese in both the English and Japanese builds.
- **Working directory:** Run-card commands run in syki::sok's own working directory. For example, `git status -s` returns the state of the folder where syki::sok was started.

Limits and details (data that is sent, and how Jev is used)

- By default, suggestions come from the built-in local rules only. Nothing from your note leaves your machine.
- Data is sent only if you set up one of the following.
- **Jev through OpenRouter:** leave the Base URL and Model Name at their defaults (`https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`, `jev-latest`) and enter an OpenRouter API key (`sk-or-v1-…`). Requests go to `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone`, which is fixed.
- **Jev at TypeSafe:** set the Base URL to `https://api.typesafe.ai` and enter your TypeSafe API key. Requests go to `https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`.
- **An OpenRouter chat model:** set the Model Name to something other than Jev (for example `google/gemini-…`) and enter an OpenRouter key. That model is asked to write the candidate text (sent to OpenRouter's `chat/completions`).
- **Your own server:** a Base URL that is none of the above receives `<Base URL>/predict`.
- There is one key field, so the kind of key is judged from the Base URL and the shape of the key (OpenRouter keys start with `sk-or-`). A TypeSafe key entered next to the OpenRouter Base URL is sent nowhere; you get the built-in candidates.
- Jev does not write text. All the built-in candidates are laid out and Jev is asked once which one fits your note best; its answer reorders them. Only built-in candidates are ever shown.
- When Jev cannot answer (a wrong key, no credit, a network error, a 5-second timeout, or low confidence), you get the built-in rules' candidates. The key is never resent to another service.
- What is sent is an excerpt around the caret: up to 1,500 characters before it and 500 after (about 2,000 in total). Nothing is sent for an empty note.
- The Base URL and Model Name fields come pre-filled with `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` and `jev-latest`, but while the API key is empty, nothing is sent.
- The safety check is the AST guardrail. The glossary explains these internal names.

---

### Editor & Split Mode (Ctrl+\)

**In one line:** Split the fast monospace Markdown editor into two panes: write on the left and watch the preview on the right. Ctrl + \ No setup needed
Split view: Markdown on the left, and a live preview with a rendered Mermaid diagram on the right

1. **Editor** The Markdown source
2. **Preview header** The note name and the pane buttons
3. **Mermaid diagram** Drawn from the code block in the note
4. **Scroll sync** Toggles whether both panes scroll together
5. **Divider** Drag to resize the panes, or move the focus to it with F6 and use the arrow keys. Double-click or Enter resets to 50:50

1. **Switch to two panes**Click the split icon in the header, or press Ctrl + \ (macOS: Cmd + \)
2. **Make the right pane a preview**The preview icon on the right pane shows the live HTML rendering
3. **Scrolling stays in sync**Scroll one pane and the other follows

To open only the preview to the side, use Ctrl + Alt + V (macOS: Cmd + Option + V). It is listed in **Settings → Shortcuts** as "Open Preview to the Side", where you can change it.

**What is shown as an HTML page:** a note whose name ends in `.html`, a note that starts with `<!DOCTYPE html>` or `<html>`, and a note that is nothing but one ````html` block are shown as an HTML page (interactive explainers and slide decks that an AI made can be viewed in the preview).

- **What works:** inline JS and CSS, data: URI images, inline SVG, canvas. Online, CDN libraries (reveal.js, Chart.js, ...) and `https://` images work too.
- **Pictures on this PC:** `<img src="assets/x.png">` (next to the note), `../x.png` (above it), an absolute path such as `C:\Users\me\a.png`, or a `file:///` address are shown (8 MB each, 24 MB in all, 12 pictures at most). A network share (`\\host\share`) is never read. A note with no file has no folder for a relative path: only absolute paths work there.
- **Good to know:** offline, a page that needs a CDN does not work; ask for "one self-contained HTML file, no external files or CDN". Click once inside the page for the arrow keys to move slides. `localStorage` and saving files are not available.
- **When an AI makes the page:** ask for "only the HTML, starting with `<!DOCTYPE html>`, no code block". If the answer is one HTML page in an ````html` block and the note it goes into is otherwise empty, the fence is taken off when it is inserted.
- **Right-click:** the editor's right-click menu has **Open Preview to the Side** as well.

**The divider.** Between two note pages the divider is a gutter: a soft shadow with dots that fade towards both sides. Beside a preview it is only the step between the page and the desk. Drag it with the mouse, or press F6 until the focus is on it (the editors keep Tab for indenting, so F6 is how the keyboard gets there, after the tab strips) and use ← / → (2 points at a time, Shift for 10), Home / End (the left page at its narrowest, 15%, or its widest, 85%) and Enter (back to half and half; a double-click does the same). Esc returns to the note. At half and half the two pages are exactly as wide as each other. The widths are not remembered: the next start is half and half again. **Settings → General → Appearance & Window → Divider between two pages** changes how it looks: gutter (the default), shadow only, or a thin line.

Find, replace, indent, and the pane commands act on

- **Find:** Ctrl + F opens the find bar (Ctrl + H adds the Replace row). Enter goes to the next match and Shift + Enter to the previous one. The focus stays in the box, so you can keep pressing Enter; these keys never change the note. While the box has the focus, the current match is drawn as a box behind the text (in a very large note it is only selected). F3 does the same from the note.
- **Replace:** Enter in the Replace box replaces the current match and moves on; **Replace all** replaces every match. Both work on the text as it is now, even if you typed in the note after searching. Each is one Ctrl + Z step, and what you typed before stays undoable.
- **Indent:** Tab and Shift + Tab on several lines indent and unindent them, again as one Ctrl + Z step.
- **Two panes:** each page has its own strip of tabs (see "Many tabs"). Commands, from the palette or a key, act on the pane you worked in last, left or right. A result that arrives after you switched notes is never put into the note you switched to.

**HTML notes:** A note that is an HTML page is shown in a sandboxed frame, and its scripts run. A link in it opens in your browser when you click it, but only `http://` and `https://` addresses open, and only after a real click. If you click a link within a few seconds of pressing a key or clicking in syki::sok itself, the status bar says "The link was not opened. Wait a moment and click it again."

---

### Comment Out Lines (Ctrl+/)

**In one line:** Hide lines in HTML comments (`<!-- -->`) and bring them back with the same key. Hidden text does not show in the preview, and a task or slot inside a comment never runs. Ctrl + / No setup needed

1. **Put the caret on a line, or select lines**Every line the selection touches is used. A selection that ends at the very start of a line leaves that line out
2. **Press Ctrl + /**(macOS: Cmd + /) Each line becomes `<!-- line -->`. The indentation stays in front: `- item` becomes `<!-- - item -->`
3. **Press it again**When every line is already a one-line comment, the comments come off. Each press is one undo step (Ctrl + Z)

- **One comment around the lines:** Settings → General → "Toggle comment writes" → "One comment around the lines" puts `<!--` before the first line and `-->` after the last. The same key takes that comment off again.
- **Lines left as they are:** empty lines, the result markers of a run (`<!-- syki:... -->`), tag lines (`<!-- tags: ... -->`, see Add and Remove Tags; they are not listed, and a selection of tag lines only says so), a line that already contains `-->` (the comment would end there) and a line that is part of a longer comment. The status bar names those lines. Nothing changes, with a message, when an unclosed `<!--` comes earlier in the note (the new `-->` would close it and hide everything in between), or when the lines are inside a code block (there `<!--` is plain text).
- **Commented-out tasks do not run:** `[[ @llm ]]`, `[[ $ ]]`, `{{ @agent }}`, the `{{ }}`-style slots and the approval gates of recipes are ignored inside a comment by Ctrl + Enter, the run button and the slot parser. With the caret inside a comment, Ctrl + Enter does nothing (it never runs another slot instead) and says so in the status bar.
- **The preview hides comments:** a line that holds only a comment disappears without splitting the paragraph around it. `<!--` inside a code block or inline code is code, and stays visible.

---

### File Links & Drag & Drop

**In one line:** Drop a file onto the text in the editor and a Markdown link is inserted at the caret. Every link in the editor is underlined, and Ctrl + click opens it (a file with its app, a web address in the browser). No setup needed
While dragging: the editor frame pulses and an "Insert as link" badge follows the pointer

1. **Pulsing frame** The editor is a drop target for the dragged file
2. **"Insert as link" badge** Dropping inserts a Markdown link to the file. A file the app cannot reference by path is first copied into the note's assets folder

1. **Drag a file**Bring it over the editor. The frame pulses and an **"Insert as link"** badge appears
2. **Drop it onto the text**Dropping onto the tab bar or the header still opens the file as a new tab, as before
3. **The link is inserted**At the caret: `![name](...)` for images, `[name](...)` for everything else. Several files give one link per line

A note with a PDF link and an image link. Point at the image link to see its thumbnail

1. **File link** Ctrl+click opens the file, and Alt+click shows it in the file manager
2. **Image link** Point at it for 0.3 seconds to see a thumbnail
3. **Thumbnail** A preview of the linked image

CtrlClickOpen the linkOpens a file or folder with the default app, and a web address in the browser. Every link in the editor is underlined (dotted for an image). macOS: Cmd + Click
AltClickShow the locationShows the file in Explorer / Finder. Web addresses do not react to Alt. macOS: Option + Click
Point at itHint and image previewRest the pointer on a link for 0.3 seconds to see how to open it. An image link also shows a thumbnail (up to 240×180)

Limits and details

- **Files are copied in:** The embedded browser does not expose the original path of a dropped file, so syki::sok copies the file (up to 25 MB each) into `./assets/` next to the note and links to it relatively. The original location is not recorded.
- **Link format:** Spaces and parentheses in the link are percent-encoded (`%20`, `%28`, `%29`), so the Markdown stays valid. Ctrl + Click still opens the file normally.
- **Links that can be opened:** `file://` links, absolute paths and note-relative paths open with the default app, and `http://` and `https://` addresses open in the browser. Other kinds of link (`mailto:`, `javascript:` and so on) are not underlined and cannot be opened from the editor.
- **What is underlined:** Markdown links `[text](...)`, images `![alt](...)` (with a dotted line, because they also preview on hover) and bare `http://` / `https://` addresses. The color is your theme's accent, a little lighter. The preview is unchanged.
- **While you hold the key:** While Ctrl (macOS: Cmd) is held, the link under the pointer gets thicker and the pointer becomes a hand, so you can see what a click will open. Alt does the same for files; web addresses do not react to Alt.
- **Hover hint:** Rest the pointer on a link for about 0.3 seconds. For a file or folder the hint reads "Ctrl+click to open / Alt+click to show its location", and for a web address "Ctrl+click to open in the browser" (macOS: Cmd+click and Option+click). A local image also shows a thumbnail (up to 240×180).
- **Images on another computer:** An image link that starts with `//` or `\\` (a network share such as `//server/share/pic.png`) is not drawn in the preview, no thumbnail is made for it, and nothing is requested from that computer. Copy the picture into the note's folder, or drop it into the note, to see it. Ctrl + Click still opens the link.
- **Long notes:** The underline is skipped for notes over 100,000 characters (Ctrl + Click still works). It is refreshed when you pause typing, not on every key.
- **macOS:** The same code runs there, with Cmd and Option in place of Ctrl and Alt. It has been checked in the Windows app so far, and not yet on a real Mac.

---

### Quick Capture (Windows)

**In one line:** A small popup for jotting something down without opening the syki::sok window. Press Ctrl + Shift + Q in any program, type, and press Enter. The text is added to today's scrap. Windows only No setup needed

Windows only

Quick Capture, its hotkey and its toolbar button exist on Windows only. On macOS the toolbar button and the shortcut row in Settings do not appear, and there is no macOS version yet.

The popup is one row: a text field and three buttons, **Send**, **AI Send** and **Capture**. It stays on top of other windows and looks dark, rounded and slightly see-through. The Send button takes the accent color of your theme. The button names stay in English in every interface language.

The Quick Capture popup: one row, floating over another program

1. **Text field** Type the note here. Leave it empty to send the text on the clipboard
2. **Send** Adds the text exactly as typed (Enter)
3. **AI Send** Corrects the text with the AI first (Ctrl + Enter)
4. **Capture** Starts a screen capture (Ctrl + Shift + Enter)

1. **Open it**Press Ctrl + Shift + Q in any program. The popup appears on top of what you are doing
2. **Type your note**A thought, a phone number, a to-do. If you leave the field empty, the text on the clipboard is used instead
3. **Press Enter**The text is added to today's scrap exactly as you typed it, and the popup closes

**Four ways to open it**

CtrlShiftQGlobal hotkeyWorks from any program. You can change it in Settings → Shortcuts
ToolbarQuick Capture buttonThe icon right after the microphone button
TrayTray menuRight-click the tray icon and choose "Quick Capture"
CtrlShiftPCommand paletteChoose "Quick Capture"

**Keys inside the popup**

EnterSendAdds the text as you typed it
CtrlEnterAI SendCorrects the text with the AI first, then adds it
CtrlShiftEnterCaptureStarts a screen capture (next section)
EscCloseCloses the popup. Text you have not sent is dropped

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Send**Enter | Adds the text exactly as typed. If the field is empty, the text on the clipboard is added instead. If both are empty, the popup just closes and nothing is added. |
| **AI Send**Ctrl + Enter | First runs the text through the same AI correction as Alt + C in the editor, then adds it. While it waits, the button reads "Working...". If you close the popup in the meantime, the note is still saved. LLM setup needed |
| **Capture**Ctrl + Shift + Enter | Captures a window or an area of the screen, reads the text in it and adds both to your note. What you typed becomes the caption. See Screen Capture (Windows). |

**Where the note goes.** Each note is added to the end of today's scrap file, `<scrap folder>/YYYY-MM-DD.md` (by default `~/Documents/syki-sok/scraps`), and is separated from the entry before it by a blank line. If that note is open in syki::sok, it updates at once. See Daily Scraps Model.

Limits and details (hotkey, closing, AI Send)

- **Change or turn off the hotkey:** Settings → Shortcuts tab, the row "Quick Capture (global, opens the note popup)". Clear the key and the hotkey is off (the toolbar button, the tray item and the palette entry keep working). If another program already uses the combination, the change is refused with a message and the previous key stays.
- **Closing by itself:** The popup closes 1 second after it loses focus. If focus comes back in time, it stays. Esc closes it at once.
- **Japanese input:** While an IME conversion is in progress, Enter and Esc go to the IME first. Confirm the conversion, then press Enter again to send.
- **Which window you were in:** When you open the popup with the hotkey and use AI Send, the entry starts with a line `> [context: <title of the window you were in>]`. Nothing is added when you open it from the toolbar, the palette or the tray, because the window in front is then syki::sok itself. A plain Send adds only your text.
- **If the AI cannot correct the text:** AI Send uses the text model in Settings → AI Models. If "Enable AI typo & error correction (Alt+C)" is off in Settings → General, if no text model is set, or if the model does not answer within 30 seconds, the text is saved as you typed it. A note is never lost or held up.

---

### Screen Capture (Windows)

**In one line:** Click a window or drag a rectangle on the screen, and syki::sok saves the picture, reads the text in it (OCR) and adds both to today's note. Start it from Quick Capture with Ctrl + Shift + Enter. Windows only

Windows only, and not for page elements

Screen Capture starts from the Quick Capture popup and exists on Windows only. There is no macOS version yet. It cannot pick a single element inside a web page (that would need a browser extension), only a window or a rectangle.

1. **Open Quick Capture**Press Ctrl + Shift + Q. If you want a caption, type it now: it is written above the picture in the note
2. **Start the capture**Click **Capture**, or press Ctrl + Shift + Enter. The popup closes, the screen dims slightly, the pointer becomes a crosshair and a hint bar appears at the top of the main monitor
3. **Pick what to capture**Point at a window and click it, or drag a rectangle (see below)
4. **Wait a few seconds**The picture is saved, then the text in it is read, and one entry is added to today's note. There is no progress display while the text is read

No picture of the whole screen is taken, and nothing is read from the screen, until you have chosen.

Picking with Ctrl held: two areas picked, a third being dragged

1. **Hint bar** The keys: click a window, drag an area, hold Ctrl to pick several, Esc to cancel
2. **Numbered green frames** What you have picked so far. They are captured in this order
3. **Green frame being dragged** Release the mouse to add it to the picks. Release Ctrl to capture them all
4. **Dimmed screen** Nothing is read from the screen until you have chosen. Esc or a right-click cancels

**Choosing what to capture**

PointClickCapture a windowA green frame shows the window under the pointer. Click to capture it
DragCapture an areaA green rectangle follows the pointer. Release to capture that area
Hold CtrlCollect severalClick or drag while holding Ctrl. Each pick gets a number badge. Release Ctrl to capture them all. Ctrl + click a picked window again to take it out
EscRight-clickCancelNothing is saved. The picker also gives up by itself after 2 minutes

**What is added to the note**

```
**[18:12:15] 画面キャプチャ**
<the caption you typed, if any>
> [context: <the window you were in>]

**1. <title of the window>**
![capture 1](./assets/2026-09-24-181328-cap1.png)
> the recognized text, one quoted line per line
```

- The header word `画面キャプチャ` ("screen capture") is Japanese in every interface language.
- The `> [context: ...]` line appears only when you opened Quick Capture with the hotkey.
- Each pick gets its own numbered block, in the order you picked. A free rectangle is labelled like `1. 選択範囲 (200×100)`: "selected area", then its width × height.
- Window titles are kept whole up to 400 characters (the title of an Explorer window is its full folder path).
- If the text cannot be read, that block has the line `> (OCRでテキストを抽出できませんでした: <reason>)` instead (Japanese in every interface language). The picture is saved before reading starts, so a failed read never loses it.

Limits and details (what can be picked, privacy, saved files)

- **What can be picked:** visible top-level windows. Not minimized windows, windows on another virtual desktop, the desktop background, tiny windows under 24 px or click-through overlays. The green frame shows the window's visible edge, without its invisible resize border.
- **How the picture is taken:** A window that is partly covered by another window, or partly off the screen, is captured from the window itself, so the covering window does not appear. Any other window, and every rectangle you drag, is read from the screen. Some apps (video players, protected content) can come out black.
- **Saved files:** Every capture is saved as a PNG in `<scrap folder>/assets/`, named `YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-cap<N>.png`, and linked from the note. You can reopen and edit it later (in Paint, for example).
- **Reading the text:** The pictures are read one after another, in the order you picked them, with the same OCR as the hot folder: the cloud vision model first, the on-device engine as the fallback.
- **Privacy:** With the default setting, the captured pictures are sent to the vision model set under Settings → AI Models → Image analysis (OCR) (Gemini and so on). To read them on your PC only, tick "Keep images on this PC" in Settings → Sync → Hot Folder section. The text is then less accurate.

---

### Hot Folder: Images & Audio to Notes

**In one line:** Put a picture or a sound file into one folder, and syki::sok reads the text in the picture (OCR) or transcribes the sound, and adds the result to today's scrap. It is off until you switch it on. Windows & macOS

Windows

- Images: the cloud vision model reads them first, and the on-device engine is the fallback
- "Keep images on this PC" reads them on the PC only
- Audio: Gemini (cloud), or Whisper on this PC (Windows x64)
- Tray menu item "Open inbox folder", and the Explorer Send To entry

macOS

- Images: the cloud vision model only. There is no on-device engine, so the "Keep images on this PC" option is hidden
- Audio: Gemini only. Whisper is not available (the settings say "On-device Whisper is only available on Windows (x64) for now.")
- There is no tray and no Send To menu. Open the folder from the command palette
- The `syki ocr` command works, with cloud OCR only

**Turn it on**

1. **Open the setting**Settings → Sync tab, the section "Hot folder"
2. **Tick the checkbox**"Watch a folder: images are OCR'd, audio is transcribed, both appended to today's scrap"
3. **Check the folder**"Watched Folder Path:" starts as `~/Documents/syki-sok/inbox`. Change it with **Browse...** if you like, then press **Save**
4. **Drop files in**Copy or move a picture or a sound file into that folder. Files that were already waiting are handled once when syki::sok starts. After that, each new file is handled as it arrives, once it has finished copying
5. **Read the result**Today's note gets a new entry. The file itself is moved into the assets folder next to your scraps

| File type | Extensions | What is added to today's note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Image** | `.png` `.jpg` `.jpeg` `.bmp` `.gif` `.webp` | The text read from the picture, as a quoted block, followed by the picture as `![name](./assets/<timestamp>-name)` |
| **Audio** | `.mp3` `.wav` `.m4a` `.ogg` `.flac` | A `**[HH:MM:SS]**` line, the transcript as a quoted block, and a link to the audio file |

Your files are moved, never deleted

A processed file is moved to `<scrap folder>/assets/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS>-<original name>`. That also happens when reading or transcribing fails. A failure leaves a line such as `> (OCRでテキストを抽出できませんでした: <reason>)` or `> (文字起こしに失敗しました: <reason>)` in the note (Japanese in every interface language), and the file is still there.

**Which engine reads the images**

- **By default:** the cloud vision model set under Settings → AI Models → Image analysis (OCR), Gemini for example, is tried first. It is far more accurate. If it fails, the on-device engine (Windows only) takes over.
- **To keep images on your PC:** tick "Keep images on this PC: read them with the on-device OCR only (less accurate)" in the same Hot Folder section. The image is then never sent out. It applies to the hot folder, Screen Capture, the Send To entry and the `ocr` command (below), but not to pasting with Ctrl + V. It is Windows only, and hidden on macOS.

**Which engine transcribes the audio**

- **The choice:** Settings → AI Models tab, the group "Voice input": the blocks **Realtime** and **Batch** each have an **Engine**: "Gemini (cloud)" (the default) or "Whisper (on this PC, offline)" (Windows x64 only, described next).
- **Where it applies:** **Batch**: the hot folder, Cloudflare Mobile Bridge, Mobile Drop and the meeting recording. **Realtime**: live Voice Input (Ctrl + Shift + R) and an audio file dropped on the window. A configuration saved before the two kinds existed keeps its engine for Batch, and Realtime stays Gemini.
- **Keys:** The voice settings reuse the API key of Image analysis (OCR) when they have none of their own.

**Opening the folder**

- **Tray menu (Windows):** right-click the tray icon and choose "Open inbox folder". It is shown only while the hot folder is on.
- **Command palette (Windows and macOS):** Ctrl + Shift + P, then "Open inbox folder" (macOS: Cmd + Shift + P). It is offered only while the hot folder is on.

Limits and details (folder, file handling, settings names)

- **Off by default:** nothing is watched until you tick the checkbox and save.
- **Timing:** files already in the folder are checked once at startup, then new files are picked up live, after their writing has settled.
- **Git sync:** If Git sync is on for the scraps folder, the pictures and audio moved into `assets/` are committed and pushed together with the notes.
- **Settings names:** in the config file, `inbox.enabled` and `inbox.dir` hold the switch and the folder, `vision.ocrMode` is empty for the default (cloud first) or `"on-device"`, and `voice.realtime.engine` and `voice.batch.engine` are `"gemini"` (the default) or `"whisper-local"`.

### On-device Whisper (Windows x64)

Whisper is a speech recognition program that runs on your own PC, so the audio is transcribed offline. It is available on 64-bit Windows only. Nothing is sent out unless you turn on the retry option under Advanced below. It works for the hot folder and the Discord Bridge only.

1. **Choose the engine**Settings → AI Models → Voice input, block **Realtime** or **Batch**, **Engine**: "Whisper (on this PC, offline)". A model to download appears in that block, and the group "Whisper (on this PC)" below holds the Whisper program (one download for both)
2. **Download the Whisper program**Press **Download** next to "Whisper program" (about 9 MB). A progress display shows how far it is. **Cancel** stops it, and the next Download continues where it stopped. **Remove** deletes the part again
3. **Choose a model and download it**Pick one under "Model" and press **Download**. The default is kotoba-whisper v2.0 quantized (about 513 MB)
4. **Save**When both parts are installed, the panel says "Ready: audio is transcribed on this PC." Press **Save**, and audio in the hot folder is transcribed on your PC

| Model | Size | Good for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| kotoba-whisper v2.0 quantized Default | about 513 MB | Japanese-specialised. A little smaller and faster than the full-precision one |
| kotoba-whisper v2.0 full precision | about 1.4 GB | Japanese-specialised, slightly more accurate. Uses more disk and memory |
| Whisper large-v3-turbo quantized | about 547 MB | Multilingual. For Japanese alone, the kotoba models are better |
| Whisper small quantized | about 181 MB | Light and fast, multilingual. Names and fast speech are more often wrong |
| Whisper base | about 141 MB | Lowest accuracy. Good for a quick test |
| Custom: a model file on this PC | - | Choose a ggml `.bin` file with **Browse...**. Pick "All Files" in the dialog to see `.bin` files |
| Custom: download from a URL | - | Enter an https address. You can also enter a SHA-256 to verify the download against (recommended) |

The names in the model list are written in Japanese in every interface language, with the size after each. The parts are stored under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\syki-sok\components`. The settings screen shows the exact path after "Stored in:".

Advanced settings and details

- **Language:** Empty means auto-detect. Examples: `ja`, `en`.
- **Threads (0 = auto):** How many processor threads it may use. 0 lets it choose.
- **Initial prompt:** Names or terms to favour, so they are recognised more reliably. The custom vocabulary of the Voice input settings is added after it (200 characters in all; terms that do not fit are left out).
- **If Whisper fails, retry with Gemini (sends the audio out):** Off by default. When on, audio that Whisper cannot transcribe (or Whisper not being installed) is sent to Gemini instead.
- **Audio formats:** Audio in m4a, mp3 and similar formats is converted on your PC before it is recognized.
- **Not on macOS:** The settings there show "On-device Whisper is only available on Windows (x64) for now."

### Send To menu and the ocr command

To read a single image on demand, without opening any window, right-click it in Explorer, or run one command. The text goes to today's scrap the same way as in the hot folder, with the same engine choice. Send To: Windows only

1. **Add the menu entry**Settings → Agent tab → "OS Integration (Send To)": press **Add**. "syki::sok (OCR)" now appears in Explorer's Send To menu. **Remove** undoes it, and a badge shows whether it is installed
2. **Send an image**Right-click an image file in Explorer, then choose Send to → syki::sok (OCR). No window opens
3. **Find the text**Its text is appended to today's note

The entry runs `syki ocr` for you. You can run it yourself in a terminal too, on Windows and macOS:

```
# Read one image and add its text to today's scrap
syki ocr C:\scans\receipt.png
# OCR text appended to C:\Users\you\Documents\syki-sok\scraps\2026-09-24.md

# Print JSON instead (put --json before the file name)
syki ocr --json C:\scans\receipt.png
```

It works while syki::sok is closed. It reads the Image analysis (OCR) settings and the scraps folder from `config.json`. It prints the path of the note, or `(no text recognized)` when there was no text. On macOS it uses cloud OCR only, and there is no Send To menu.

---

### Live Mermaid Diagrams & Image Rendering

**In one line:** A diagram written in a ````mermaid` block is drawn right in the preview. You can also export it as a high-resolution PNG image.

Drawn in the preview No setup needed

- Flowcharts, sequence diagrams and Gantt charts written in ````mermaid` are supported
- They are rendered as diagrams in real time in the preview
- When AI makes the diagram from your text ("Diagram: Convert Selection to Mermaid"), a text about one subject gives one diagram. A text with separate parts (a process and a data model, independent flows, or a flow too large for one picture) is split into up to four diagrams, each with its own title and the type that fits it best
- The usual slips of the AI in a diagram (a fence tagged ```timeline instead of ```mermaid, a label with parentheses, Japanese attribute names in an ER diagram, ...) are put right by rule before the diagram is inserted. A diagram that fails to draw gets the same repair and is drawn once more (the note itself is not changed)
- If a diagram is hard to read, press the half-filled circle at its top-right corner to switch between dark and light. A light diagram is drawn on a white card. The choice is kept

Diagram to image Gemini key needed

- Right-click a diagram and choose **"Render Image..."**
- It works with Gemini (Nano Banana 2 Lite) and exports a high-resolution PNG image

Limits and details (image settings)

- Choose the model, aspect ratio and resolution under "Image generation" in Settings → AI Models.
- If the Gemini API key field is empty, the Vision key is used, then the Text key, in that order.
- The image is saved as `assets/diagram_<number>.png`, and `![Generated Diagram](assets/diagram_...png)` is inserted. Save the note first to get a relative link.
- A note that is not saved yet has no folder, so the link holds the full path of the app's own `assets` folder (on macOS, under `~/Library/Application Support/syki-sok`). A space in it is written as `%20`, and the preview turns it back into the real path.
- Diagram colors: the button on each diagram switches dark and light. Settings → General → "Diagram (Mermaid) colors" also offers Gray and Green, both on a white card.

---

### Print or Save the Preview as PDF

**In one line:** Press the printer button at the top right of the preview to print the note, or to save it as a PDF, on a white page in black text whatever your theme. Windows opens syki::sok's own print panel; macOS opens its own print dialog. Windows: panel macOS: system dialog
The print panel on Windows: the pages on the left, the settings on the right

1. **Printed page** The page as it will be printed: white paper, black text, diagrams in light colours
2. **Paper, orientation, margins, scale** Paper (A4, A3, B5, Letter), orientation, margins and scale. Every change makes a new preview
3. **Header and footer** Off by default. When on: the file name above, the folder and the page number below
4. **Save as PDF** Asks where to save the file. Print... is the system print dialog, for a printer

1. **Open the preview**Show the note's Markdown preview: the preview icon of the toolbar or Ctrl + P (macOS: Cmd + P), or Ctrl + Alt + V (macOS: Cmd + Option + V) to open it to the side
2. **Press the printer button**It sits at the top right of the preview, to the left of the "Preview" tag (its tooltip reads "Print or save as PDF"). For a preview opened beside the editor it is in the header of that pane, between the scroll-sync and the Editor / Preview buttons, and it prints the note that pane shows. On Windows the print panel opens
3. **Choose how it should look**Paper (A4, A3, B5, Letter), orientation, margins (Normal or Narrow), scale and pages (for example `1-3, 5`; empty means all). The page on the left follows every change. The header and footer switch is off by default: switched on, the top has the note's file name and the bottom has the folder it is saved in, with the page number at the right (a note that is not a file yet says "(not saved yet)")
4. **Save or print****Save as PDF** asks where to save (the note's name is offered) and writes a PDF; no printer or driver is involved. **Print...** opens the system's print dialog, for a printer

Limits and details (the paper look, margins, memory, macOS, the command line)

- **The paper look:** only the preview is printed (no tabs, tool bar or status bar), on a white page in black text, whatever the theme. Headings, quotes, code and tables get plain black-and-grey rules. Pictures are printed in colour. A picture or a diagram is never wider than the page (a smaller one is not enlarged) and never taller than a page, and it moves whole to the next page instead of being cut. A Mermaid diagram in the dark tone is drawn again in the light tone for the print, and goes back afterwards. Code wraps, table rows are not cut, and a line that introduces a picture stays with it. A diagram that is wider than a portrait page shrinks to fit; choosing landscape makes it larger.
- **Margins:** Normal is 20 mm and Narrow is 10 mm. Your choices are remembered, except the page range.
- **Memory:** nothing is loaded or kept until the first press: the print style applies to printing only and the scripts are loaded on the first press. While the panel is open, the PDF viewer takes about 170 MB of working memory; closing the panel gives it back, and the PDF is not kept.
- **macOS:** the same button opens macOS's own print dialog instead of the panel. Choose **PDF → Save as PDF** at its lower left to save a PDF (the note's name is offered as the file name), or pick a printer. Paper, orientation and scale are set in that dialog. The margin is 20 mm, and there is no header or footer. It needs macOS 11 or later and has not yet been confirmed on a real Mac.
- **HTML pages:** the button is not shown in the editor or over an HTML page; an HTML page cannot be printed this way.
- **From the command line (Windows only):** `syki tab pdf notes.md -o notes.pdf` makes the same PDF with the running app. It never replaces a PDF that is already there unless you add `--overwrite`, and the window flickers briefly while the preview is shown. See Headless CLI Commands for the options. The JSON-RPC method is `print.pdf` (see JSON-RPC 2.0 API Specification).

---

### Parallel Daily Scrap Search (Ctrl+Shift+F)

**In one line:** Find a word across tens of thousands of lines of past daily scraps in under 150 ms, then click a result to jump straight to that line. Ctrl + Shift + F No setup needed
Ctrl + Shift + F: the results for "API"

1. **Search box** Searches every daily scrap as you type
2. **File name and line number** Where the match is
3. **Matching line** Shown with the line before and after it. Enter or a click opens the file at that line, and Tab inserts the line into your note

1. **Open the search modal**Ctrl + Shift + F (macOS: Cmd + Shift + F). The text you selected, or with nothing selected the word just before the caret, is already in the search box and searched
2. **Type a word**It searches across all past daily scraps. Change the query if the first guess is not what you wanted
3. **Click a result line**You jump straight to that line (Enter does the same)
4. **Or quote the line**Press Tab (or Shift + Enter) on a result and that line is inserted at the caret of your note, without leaving it. It replaces a selection, like a paste, and Ctrl + Z undoes it

Limits and details

It uses all available CPU cores (`runtime.NumCPU()`) to run a multithreaded, case-insensitive substring search (plain text, not a regular expression) across your historical scraps.

- The search works line by line, so a selection of several lines starts the search with its first line.
- When no line holds the whole text, the notes that hold its words (any lines, any order) are listed instead, best first, under a short note that says so. A search that finds a line works exactly as before.
- The word before the caret is the last word of the line up to the caret: a Latin word (`ESP32`, `foo/bar.go`) or a run of katakana and kanji. A trailing particle or ending in hiragana and the punctuation after the word are skipped, so `ESP32のピン配置なんだっけ？` starts the search with `ピン配置`.
- Text selected in the preview also counts. Tab needs the editor to be visible: while the preview covers it, it shows a message instead.
- Enter, Tab and the arrow keys are left to the IME while a conversion is open.
- Ctrl + F (find in the note) also starts with the selected text, in the editor or in the preview; several lines give the first line.
- The **Filter** button under the box narrows the search to a period and to tags (see Filter by Period and Tags).

### Filter by Period and Tags

**In one line:** Narrow a notes search to a period and to the tags in your notes (written by hand, or added with a command). The same filter applies to the Exact search, the Meaning search and Deep search. No setup needed
Ctrl + Shift + F with the Filter area open: Last 30 days and the tag "work" chosen

1. **Filter button** Opens and closes the filter. While something is chosen it shows how many choices are on, for example Filter (2)
2. **Period** One at a time: All, Today, Last 7 days, Last 30 days or This month. It goes by the date at the start of the file name
3. **Tags** The tags written in your notes, most notes first. Choose several and a note must have all of them
4. **Clear** Appears while something is chosen and takes every choice off at once

1. **Open the search and type**Ctrl + Shift + F (macOS: Cmd + Shift + F). The filter narrows a search, so there has to be a word or a question in the box
2. **Press Filter**The button is under the search box. The area opens with the periods and the tags. The tags are read from your notes the first time you open it, and not before
3. **Choose a period, tags, or both**The search runs again each time. Press a chosen tag again to let it go, choose **All** to drop the period, or press **Clear** to take everything off. When nothing matches, the list says "No notes match the filter"
4. **Search as usual**Exact, Meaning and **Deep search** all use the filter. Deep search sends only what the filtered list shows, never an excerpt that does not pass the filter. The choice stays while syki::sok is open, so the next search is narrowed the same way

**Write a tag into a note**

A tag is a whole line that is an HTML comment. The preview and the print never show it, and it stays in the note's own file. You can type the line yourself, as below, or let a command of the palette write it (see Add and Remove Tags).

```
<!-- tags: travel -->
# Osaka trip

## Hotel
<!-- tags: booking -->
Two nights near the station.

### Breakfast
Rice, miso soup and grilled fish.

## Food
Find a good takoyaki place.
```

The first line is above the first heading, so `travel` belongs to the whole note. The second comment is under the Hotel heading, so `booking` belongs to Hotel and also to the smaller heading below it, Breakfast, but not to Food. Filtering by `travel` finds every entry of the note; filtering by `travel` and `booking` finds Hotel and Breakfast. This is how a Web article pasted under a heading, and cut into several entries by its own `##` and `###` headings, is tagged with one line.

Limits and details (how a tag is written, what it covers, the period, what is read)

- **How to write it:** the whole line is `<!-- tags: a, b -->` (the key may also be `tag`, in any case). Separate the tags with commas (`,` or `、`), semicolons or spaces. A leading `#` is dropped, capitals become lower case and full-width letters half-width, so `#Work` and `work` are one tag; hiragana and katakana are not made the same. A comment holds up to 32 tags, and a tag longer than 64 characters is ignored.
- **Whole note, one heading and what is under it:** a tag line above the first heading or `---` rule of the note tags the whole note. Anywhere else it tags the entry it is in: the part between two headings (`#` to `###`) or `---` rules, the same entries the search cuts out. It also applies to every entry under that heading: the smaller headings that follow it, up to the next heading of the same or a higher level or the next `---` rule (an entry may skip a level, `#` then `###`). `####` and deeper headings are not boundaries: they are text of the entry above. A hit has a tag when its own entry has it, a heading above it has it, or the whole note has it. A tag does not reach a sibling heading, a heading of a higher level or anything after a `---` rule (a rule starts a new outline: nothing above it reaches below it). To tag one section only, put the line under that section's own heading; to tag everything, put it above the first heading.
- **Front matter:** a YAML front matter at the very top of a file (`---`, then `tags: [a, b]`, `tags: a, b` or `tags:` with a list of `- a` lines, then `---`) tags the whole note too. syki::sok reads it and never writes it, so the tag commands cannot add a whole-note tag to such a note or take one out of its front matter.
- **What is not read:** a tag comment inside a code block, in the middle of a line, or in a comment that runs over several lines. A tag line is also left out of the lines shown around a hit, as it is in the preview (the line can still be the hit itself).
- **All of the chosen tags:** a note must have every tag you chose. You can choose up to 8 at once; with 8 chosen the other buttons cannot be pressed. A tag that nobody uses simply finds nothing. The list shows the 40 tags in the most notes and counts the rest ("N more"); hover a tag to see how many notes have it. With no tag in any note yet, the area says how to write one.
- **Period:** it uses the date at the start of the file name: `2026-09-27.md` and `2026-09-27_title.md` are both 27 September 2026. Last 7 days is today and the 6 days before, Last 30 days is today and the 29 days before, and This month is the 1st to today. A note whose name does not start with a date is never inside a period, and while a period is chosen the area says how many such notes there are. A date in a heading, or the time a file was changed, is not used.
- **It lasts while the app is open:** the choice is not saved, so after a restart the filter is empty. The area starts closed each time you open the search, and the tag list is read again when you open it, so a tag you have just written appears after you close the search and open it again.
- **Costs nothing until used:** a search with no filter works exactly as before, and your notes are not read for tags until you open the Filter area (or search with a tag chosen).
- **macOS:** the code is the same, but it has not yet been verified on a real Mac.
- **The same filter elsewhere:** `syki scrap search --tag work,urgent` and `syki scrap tags` on the command line, and the `tag` parameter of `scrap.search` and the method `scrap.tags` in JSON-RPC (see Headless CLI Commands). `syki scrap tag` and `scrap.tag_edit` add and remove tags the same way as the palette commands.

### Add and Remove Tags

**In one line:** Put a tag on the entry your caret is in, on a heading and everything under it (a pasted Web article, for one), or on the whole note, from the command palette, and take it off again. syki::sok writes the hidden tag line for you, in one step you can undo. No setup needed
Command palette → Add a tag to this entry, with the new tag "release" typed

1. **Which entry** The chip says what gets the tag: the entry that holds the caret line, with its lines and the heading the tag line will go under (here "Entry, lines 9-13" and the heading `[10:24:07] Release notes draft`). An entry is the part from one heading (`#` to `###`) or `---` rule to the next, so the tag can go well above the caret. The whole-note command says "Whole note" here. After you press Enter the status line says where the tag went: the heading, the line, and how far above or below the cursor that is
2. **Input** Type a tag, or several separated by a comma, a space or a semicolon. A leading `#` is dropped
