3. **Tags** What you typed as "New tag", then the tags found in your notes folder that fit what you typed (the whole list while the box is empty), most notes first, with the number of notes. Enter or a click applies the chosen row

1. **Put the caret in the entry, or select a word**Click into the entry you want to tag. To use a word of the text as the tag, select that word first. With a selection over several lines, the tag goes under the heading that both the first and the last selected line are under, so selecting a whole pasted article tags the article as a whole. The command works on the note in the editor you were working in (the focused pane when the view is split); with the preview covering the editor it asks you to switch to the editor first
2. **Open the command palette and type "tag", or right-click the note**Ctrl + Shift + P (macOS: Cmd + Shift + P). Choose **Add a tag to this entry**, or **Add a tag to the whole note** to tag every entry of the note at once. The same three commands are in the right-click menu of the editor, under Voice input (right-click on the entry you mean: the entry is the one the caret lands in). There is no extra shortcut
3. **Type a tag, or pick one**The list narrows as you type, and the arrow keys move the highlight. A word you selected in step 1 is already in the box, all of it selected: Enter adds it, typing replaces it and Backspace empties the box. Enter (or Tab, or a click on the row) adds the highlighted row. Esc closes the picker and gives the caret back to the editor
4. **Choose where it attaches (only when there is a choice)**An entry that has headings above it gets an **Attach to** row: its own heading and each heading above it, each with its lines, such as "Processing (10-13)" and "[10:24:07] About bamboo (3-15)". Click one, or press Ctrl + Up for the heading above and Ctrl + Down to go back. The tag goes directly under the chosen heading and reaches everything below it; the line above the list says so, for example "Entry and everything under it (3 entries), lines 3-15". With nothing to choose between, the row is not shown
5. **See the result**A line `<!-- tags: ... -->` appears and flashes in the amber band, and the status bar says what was done, and, when the heading has entries below it, "It also applies to the N entries under it." Ctrl + Z (macOS: Cmd + Z) takes the whole change back in one step, and Redo applies it again
6. **To take a tag off**Choose **Remove a tag** in the palette (or in the right-click menu). Pick the heading in the **Take off from** row if there is one. The list holds the tags written at that heading, the tags that come from a heading above (marked From "Heading" (line N); choosing one takes it off at that heading) and the tags of the whole note; Enter removes the highlighted one. When the last tag of a line goes, the line goes too

For example, with the caret in the Hotel entry, **Add a tag to this entry** and the tag `booking` turn this:

```
## Hotel
Two nights near the station.
```

into this. The preview and the print show no difference:

```
## Hotel
<!-- tags: booking -->
Two nights near the station.
```

**A Web article, or any entry with smaller headings under it**

A Web article pasted under a heading is often cut into several entries by its own `###` headings, and one tag line tags it all. With the caret in one of its sections, the picker offers the section's own heading and the heading above it; choose the heading above (a click, or Ctrl + Up) and the tag goes there and reaches every section below it. Select the whole article (or start the selection at its top heading) and the picker opens already on that heading.

Command palette → Add a tag to this entry, then Ctrl + Up moves the tag from the Processing section to the article's heading

1. **What gets the tag** The chosen heading and everything under it: how many entries are below it, their lines and the heading the tag line will go under. For an entry with nothing under it, the chip reads "Entry, lines ..." as in the first picture
2. **Attach to** The entry's own heading and each heading above it, each with its lines. The lit one is chosen; click another, or press Ctrl + Up (the heading above) and Ctrl + Down (back toward the entry). The row appears only when there is more than one place. When you remove a tag it reads "Take off from"
3. **Tags** What you typed as "New tag", then the tags of the notes folder that fit it, with the number of notes. Enter or a click puts the chosen tag under the chosen heading

For example, in the note of the picture the tag `bamboo`, attached to the article's heading, turns this:

```
## [10:24:07] About bamboo
Clipped from a web page.

### Growth
```

into this, with the line directly under the article's heading:

```
## [10:24:07] About bamboo
<!-- tags: bamboo -->
Clipped from a web page.

### Growth
```

Growth, Processing and Uses now have the tag too, so filtering by `bamboo` finds the article's top part and all three sections. To tag Processing alone, leave **Attach to** on Processing: the line then goes under `### Processing` and reaches nothing else.

Limits and details (where the line goes, what is refused, undo, the command line)

- **Which entry, and where it attaches:** by default the one that holds the caret line: the part between two headings (`#` to `###`) or `---` rules, the same entries the search cuts out. With a selection over several lines it is the lowest heading that both the first and the last selected line are under (a selection inside one entry stays on that entry; one that spans separate articles falls back to the entry of its first line). The **Attach to** row lists that entry's own heading and each heading above it, and the tag goes under the one you choose and reaches everything below that heading. A caret above the note's first heading or rule, or in a note with no heading at all, is in the whole note: the chip says "Whole note" and the tag goes on the whole note.
- **Where the line goes:** one line, `<!-- tags: a, b -->`. For an entry it goes directly under the heading; when the entry starts with a `---` rule and a `## [time] title` heading (the shape a piped command writes into the daily scrap), under that heading. For the whole note it goes on the very first line of the note. When the range already has such a line, the tag is added to it instead of a second line being made. Only the chosen heading gets a line: the entries below it are not touched, they get the tag through the heading.
- **Not added twice:** a tag the entry already has, also through a whole-note tag or a heading above it, is not written again, and the status bar says "Already there". Tags are written in the form the search compares: no `#`, lower case, full-width letters made half-width.
- **Nothing else changes:** every other character of the note stays as it was, line endings and a byte order mark included. If the note changed while the request was running, nothing is applied and the message asks you to try again.
- **Refused, with a sentence of its own and nothing changed:** a note that starts with a YAML front matter (`---` at the very top) cannot get a whole-note tag, because the line cannot go above it and under it would mean something else; tag an entry instead, or write `tags:` in the front matter yourself. A tag that exists only in the front matter cannot be removed by the command, because syki::sok never writes a front matter. A tag that sits on the other range is reported ("it is on the whole note", "it is on the entry") and left alone: choose **Remove a tag** and pick the one marked with that range. A tag that a section only gets from a heading above it cannot be taken off the section itself: the status line says which heading it is written under and its line; take it off there (pick that heading in **Take off from**, or the tag marked From "Heading"), and it goes from everything under that heading.
- **Limits:** at most 8 tags at a time and 64 characters for one tag, and a tag cannot contain `-->` or `<!--`. The picker says which limit you passed instead of dropping the extra tags quietly.
- **Comment Out Lines leaves tag lines alone:** Ctrl + / (macOS: Cmd + /) neither comments a tag line out nor takes its comment off, since it would stop being a tag. A selection of tag lines only does nothing and says so (see Comment Out Lines).
- **A selected word as the tag:** when you add a tag, a single word selected on one line (200 characters or fewer) is filled into the box and selected. A leading `#`, quotes, brackets and the punctuation around it are trimmed first. Two words, a selection over several lines or a word that cannot be a tag (over 64 characters, or holding `-->`) are not filled in, and the box starts empty. Removing never fills it.
- **Not available:** AI suggestions of tags, tagging many notes at once, writing into a front matter, and moving a tag from one heading to another (take it off, then add it again).
- **macOS:** the code is the same, but it has not yet been verified on a real Mac. Ctrl + Up is a Mission Control shortcut there, so click the heading in the Attach to row instead.
- **The same from a script:** `syki scrap tag add|remove <tags> [<file>] [--line N] [--write]` and `scrap tag show` on the command line, and the method `scrap.tag_edit` in JSON-RPC, which works the edit out from the text you send and touches no file and no tab (see Headless CLI Commands). `--line` may be any line of the section; to tag a whole pasted article, give a line of its top heading.

### Meaning Search (experimental, off by default)

**In one line:** Find a note by what it says, not by its words. Ask in your own words ("the idea about sustainable building materials") and the note about bamboo comes first, in Japanese, English or both. It is off until you switch it on in `config.json`. Setup needed

**Turn it on (once)**

Settings → AI Models → Semantic search (at the end of the tab)

1. **The switch** Turn on semantic search. It fills in the usual local model (Ollama, `bge-m3`)
2. **The embedding model** Its server and its name. A cloud model also needs an API key
3. **Where your notes go** This PC (green), or a cloud host (amber), which you must allow with the box that appears
4. **The index** How many notes are in it and how far it is behind
5. **Update now** Makes the index, or brings it up to date. Rebuild makes it again from scratch

1. **Get the model**Run `ollama pull bge-m3`. A model on this PC is the default choice; a cloud embedding model works too (see the details below)
2. **Turn it on in Settings**Open Settings (Ctrl + ,; macOS: Cmd + ,), the **AI Models** tab, and open **Semantic search** at the end of the tab (turn on **Show advanced** to open every section). Turn on the switch
3. **Press Update now**syki::sok sends the text of your notes to the embedding model and makes the index; you see the progress and can **Stop** it (what was done is kept). Later updates read only the notes that are new or changed. It works before you press Save
4. **Press Save**The notes search now has an **Exact | Meaning** switch. No restart is needed

The same index is made by `syki scrap index` on the command line, and you can still write the setting by hand in `config.json` (with syki::sok closed):

```
"semantic": {
  "enabled": true,
  "model": { "baseUrl": "http://localhost:11434", "model": "bge-m3" }
}
```

Ctrl + Shift + F in Meaning mode: a question in other words than the notes use

1. **Exact | Meaning switch** Meaning finds notes close in meaning, even when they use other words
2. **Question box** Write the question in your own words
3. **Notes closest in meaning** Best first, with no score shown. Enter opens the file at that line
4. **Deep search** Sends excerpts of these notes to the AI and writes an answer with source links into a new note (Ctrl + Enter). It asks first

1. **Open the search**Ctrl + Shift + F (macOS: Cmd + Shift + F)
2. **Choose Meaning**Click **Meaning** in the **Exact | Meaning** switch. Exact finds the words you type; Meaning finds notes close in meaning
3. **Write the question in your own words**The search starts a moment after you stop typing. You do not need the words of the note: "the idea about sustainable building materials" finds the note about bamboo
4. **Open the note**Press Enter (or click) on a result to open the note at that line. Tab inserts the line into your note, as in the plain search

Limits and details (how many notes, what is left out, where the model runs, the index)

- **10 notes:** the list shows 10 notes; **Show more** asks for 30. No score is shown. Notes that score far below the best one are left out, and a quiet line under the list says how many.
- **Notes not in the index yet:** notes written after the last `syki scrap index` are searched by their words, and a line under the list says how many. Run the command again to bring them in.
- **When Meaning cannot be used** (for example the model cannot be reached), the notes are picked by their words and a line says so.
- **Where the model runs:** on this PC by default. A model that is not on this PC is used only for a host you have allowed (the box that appears under the model in Settings; it is kept in `semantic.privacy.cloudConsent` in `config.json`); until then nothing is sent to it, and Update now stays disabled.
- **The index:** it is kept on this PC, outside the scraps folder, is never Git-synced and may be deleted at any time (`syki scrap index` makes it again). An exported settings package never carries the `semantic` section.
- **Costs nothing while it is off:** with the switch off (or no `semantic` section in `config.json`) the notes search is the plain panel.
- **macOS:** it is expected to work, because the code is the same, but it has not yet been verified on a real Mac.
- **The same search elsewhere:** `syki scrap search --semantic` on the command line and the JSON-RPC method `scrap.search` (see Headless CLI Commands).

### Deep Search

**In one line:** In Meaning mode, press **Deep search** and the AI reads excerpts of the notes that were found and writes one answer, with numbered sources that link back to the notes, into a new unsaved note. A dialog shows what would be sent, and where, first; no excerpt goes to the AI until you press **Run**. Text LLM needed
The Deep search dialog: what would be sent, and where, before you press Run

1. **What will be sent** The number of notes, about how many characters, and whether the model is on this computer or in the cloud
2. **Sources** The notes whose excerpts are sent, with how many characters of each. The list is folded until you press "Sources"
3. **Left out, blanked out** What was left out, and how many secrets (keys, tokens, passwords) are blanked out before sending
4. **Cancel** Sends nothing
5. **Run** Sends the excerpts and opens the answer in a new note

1. **Search by meaning**Open the notes search (Ctrl + Shift + F), choose **Meaning** and ask your question. The notes on screen are where Deep search starts
2. **Press Deep search**Click the button at the right of the search box, or press Ctrl + Enter (macOS: Cmd + Enter) while the list is on screen. syki::sok searches again and cuts the passage around each hit out of its note. Nothing is sent yet
3. **Read the dialog**It says how many notes and about how many characters (and roughly how many tokens) would go, to which model, whether that model is on this computer or in the cloud, what was left out and why, and how many secrets were blanked out
4. **Press Run**The excerpts go to the model. It runs as a task in the Task panel (Alt + T; macOS: Option + T), where you can cancel it. If the model is on a host you have not allowed yet, the dialog first asks "Excerpts of your notes will be sent over the internet to <host>. Allow it?" and the button reads **Allow and run**

**What you get**

The answer opens in a **new, unsaved note** titled "Deep search <your question>". Save it, or close it and nothing is kept. It holds:

- the question, as the heading;
- the answer, with numbers such as `[1]` and `[2]` that point to the sources;
- a **Sources** list: one link to each note (Ctrl + Click, macOS Cmd + Click, opens it) with the lines of the excerpt written beside it. A source the answer did not use says so. syki::sok makes the links, not the AI: the AI is never asked to write one, and a number that is no source is dropped;
- a few quoted lines. A quotation that cannot be found in the note it names is marked `(unverified)`;
- a foot saying which model answered, when, and whether the notes were found by meaning or by words.

Privacy and limits (what is sent, where, and for how long)

- **No excerpt is sent before Run.** The dialog only shows what would go, and Cancel sends nothing. Enter in the first moments after the dialog opens is ignored, because it is the key that opened it. Prepared excerpts expire after 15 minutes; syki::sok then prepares them again.
- **Secrets are blanked out:** a key, token or password found in an excerpt is blanked out before sending, and the dialog counts them.
- **What is never sent:** notes excluded by `.syki-ignore`, `.syki-ignore` or the folder rules, hidden folders, AI result blocks, earlier Deep search notes, files that cannot be read and what is over the size limit. The dialog lists what was left out.
- **With a filter on:** when a period or tags are chosen in the Filter, Deep search gathers its excerpts under the same filter, and the neighbouring entries it adds to a short excerpt must pass it too. Nothing outside the filter is planned for sending.
- **This PC or another host:** only a model on this PC itself (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`) counts as local. A model anywhere else, a machine on your local network included, asks for your consent once per host: **Allow and run** remembers it in the same allowed-hosts list as the Ask bar. syki::sok checks that saved consent again when it runs.
- **Which model:** the Text LLM of Settings → AI Models, the one the Ask AI bar uses. Both its address and its model name must be set; otherwise the dialog says "No AI model is set up yet." with a **Set up** button. If Meaning search is not available, the notes are picked by their words and the dialog says so.
- **Time:** a run takes up to 9 minutes at most, and can be cancelled in the Task panel.
- **Never in your scraps by itself:** the answer is only in the new tab. Nothing is written into the scraps folder unless you save it there.
- **From a script:** the JSON-RPC method `deepsearch.plan` is a dry run that says which notes would go and where; it sends nothing. `ui.open_panel` can open the notes search in Meaning mode for you. No method runs a deep search: you press the button.

---

### Mobile Drop · Send from your phone (Ctrl+Shift+U)

**In one line:** Scan a QR code with your phone and send photos, voice notes, text or URLs, or a small text file to the note on your PC. No app and no account needed. Ctrl + Shift + U

**Phone**Scan the QR code

**Phone**Pick photos, a voice note or text, and send

**PC**Appended to the end of the note, with one heading per item

The dialog on the PC: QR code, address, the selection shared with the phone, and the time left (the QR code and address are demo values)

1. **QR code** Scan it with the phone camera (phone and PC on the same Wi-Fi / LAN)
2. **Address** The one-time address behind the QR code
3. **Sharing with phone** The text selected in the editor is shown on the phone (the "Text from PC" card)
4. **Countdown** Time until the idle timeout. When it runs out, the dialog closes and the address stops working (activity on the phone extends it)
5. **Switch to an outside connection** An optional switch to a Cloudflare tunnel, for mobile data or another Wi-Fi

1. **Open the dialog**Click the phone icon in the toolbar, press Ctrl + Shift + U (macOS: Cmd + Shift + U), or choose **Mobile Drop** in the Command Palette
2. **Scan the QR code with the phone camera**The phone must be on the same Wi-Fi (the same LAN) as the PC. The address is also shown as text under the code, so you can type it in
3. **Fill the send tray**Add photos or files (up to 10 items, 60 MB total), a voice note and text, in any combination
4. **Press "Send all"**There is only one button. An upload progress indicator shows while it sends
5. **It is appended to the note**The dialog closes and the content is appended to the end of the active note. Each item gets its own heading: `## Mobile Drop [14:20:05] — <filename>`

**The page that opens on the phone**

The top of the page on the phone (every label shows Japanese and English together)

1. **Text from PC** The text selected on the PC. Tap the button below it to copy it on the phone
2. **Send tray** Everything you have added so far (a photo and a note file here). ✕ removes an item
3. **Take a photo** Takes a photo with the phone camera
4. **Choose files** Pick photos or text files from the phone (several at once)
5. **Record voice** Opens the phone's own recorder. The recording is added to the tray and transcribed on the PC

The same page scrolled to the bottom

1. **Text or URL box** Paste a note or a link to send it as text
2. **Send all** Sends the tray and the text to the active note on the PC in one go (one submission per session)

| On the phone | What ends up in the note |
| --- | --- |
| Photos / files | Photos are transcribed to Markdown by the vision model. `.md` and `.txt` are added as they are; `.html`, `.js`, `.json`, `.py` and other code or config files are wrapped in a fenced code block. Shift_JIS text files are converted automatically. |
| Voice note | Transcribed the same way as Voice Input and added as text. |
| Text or URL | The text exactly as typed or pasted. A lone URL becomes a Markdown link. |

**Where photos and voice notes go**

API set up

- **Photos:** The same vision model as Ctrl + V image OCR (Settings → AI Models → Image analysis (OCR)) transcribes them to Markdown. The photo itself is not saved
- **Voice notes:** Transcribed the same way as Voice Input (the same Gemini model) and added as text
- A local (Ollama or LM Studio) vision model does OCR even without a key

Not set up, or it fails

- Whether the key is missing, the model is not supported, the transcript is empty, or there is an HTTP error or a timeout, the photo or voice note is **not lost**
- It is saved to `./assets/` just like an image pasted with Ctrl + Shift + V, and the note gets a link plus a one-line reason
- A toast tells you how many items were handled this way

Limits and details (the lines added when an item is saved, and where)

When an item is saved, one of these lines goes into the note, depending on the situation. These inserted lines are Japanese in both UI languages.

| Situation | Photo | Voice note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nothing is configured | `![name](./assets/...)` and `> 画像OCRをスキップし、画像として保存しました: <error> (設定 → AIモデル → 画像解析)` | `[name](./assets/...)` and `> 文字起こしをスキップし、音声として保存しました: <error> (設定 → AIモデル → 音声入力)` |
| Any other failure | `> 画像OCRに失敗したため、画像として保存しました: <error>` | `> 文字起こしに失敗したため、音声として保存しました: <error>` |

- **Where it is saved:** `./assets/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmmss.<extension>`, next to the note. If there is no saved note, the workspace folder; if that is missing too, the app data folder (then the link is a `file://` link). A name collision appends `-2`, `-3`.
- **If saving fails too:** Only when saving to assets fails as well, `[Mobile Drop: <filename> の処理に失敗しました: <error>]` is appended after that item's heading. The remaining items arrive normally.

Limits and details (what you can send, and size limits)

- Up to 10 photos or files, 60 MB in total.
- Per-item limits: an image 20 MB, an audio file 25 MB, a text file 2 MB. Any other binary file is refused.

Limits and details (the phone page and "Text from PC")

- **Page layout:** From top to bottom: the "Text from PC" card, the "Send tray" (each added item shows its name, size and a `✕` to remove it), camera / file picker (several files) / voice recording, and the text box. There is only one send button.
- **"Text from PC":** The text selected on the PC (or the clipboard text, if nothing was selected when the dialog opened) is shown with a one-tap copy button. It refreshes every 2 seconds and shows up to 64 KB.
- **On the PC:** The dialog shows it as "Sharing with phone: ...", truncated to 80 characters.

**Choose a connection**

Same Wi-Fi (LAN) Default

- The phone and the PC must be on the same network
- Nothing leaves that network
- For voice notes, the phone's own recorder app opens
- Location is neither requested nor attached

Via Cloudflare (mobile data, another Wi-Fi)

- Press **"Connect from outside via Cloudflare (mobile data / other Wi-Fi)"** in the dialog
- It opens an account-free Cloudflare Quick Tunnel, and the QR code switches to a temporary `https://…trycloudflare.com` address
- For voice notes, you can record right in the page (HTTPS)
- Location can optionally be attached, once
- The transferred data passes through Cloudflare's servers

Limits and details (the Cloudflare tunnel)

- It needs `cloudflared`. syki::sok never downloads or installs it for you.
- If it is missing, the dialog shows the install command (Windows: `winget install --id Cloudflare.cloudflared -e`, macOS: `brew install cloudflared`) with a **Copy** button. Run it, then press the button again.
- While the tunnel is up, the transferred data passes through Cloudflare's servers.
- **About the 90 seconds:** The tunnel's 90 seconds is an idle timeout. Activity on the phone re-arms it. It is not a fixed "valid for 90 seconds after it is issued" limit.

Limits and details (safety and limits)

- **It exists only while the dialog is open.** Opening it starts a small server on the PC. It stops after one submission, after 60 seconds without activity, or when you close or cancel the dialog. Opening the page on the phone, and any work on the phone (adding a file, recording, typing), all count as activity and reset that timer. So even a large batch does not trip the 60-second idle timeout.
- **One submission per QR code.** To send more, open the dialog again. The one-time token is checked before the request body is even read.
- **Only someone with the code can send.** The address contains a random one-time token, and a request without it is refused before anything is read.
- **Photos and cloud models.** If your vision model is a cloud service such as Gemini, photos are sent to that provider, exactly as when you paste an image with Ctrl + V. Even with no API key, the photo is not lost: it is saved as an image (see "Not set up, or it fails" above).
- **Location is opt-in and tunnel-only.** Only when connected through the Cloudflare tunnel (HTTPS), the phone may attach its location once, as a single one-time attempt. Only the first item's heading carries it: `## Mobile Drop [14:20:05] — <filename> (34.693, 135.502)`. Over plain LAN HTTP, location is never requested or attached.

Limits and details (how sending survives interruptions)

On a plain LAN connection, recording a voice note opens the phone's own recorder app. To keep the session alive meanwhile, the phone page works as follows.

- Just before handing over to the camera, the file picker or the recorder app, it asks the PC to keep the session open up to 120 seconds longer. The PC session normally ends after 60 seconds without activity, and the server caps such a request at 180 seconds.
- When you come back to the page, it pings the PC.
- A picked file is copied into memory right away, because recorder apps may still be writing to it or may revoke access.
- While files are being read, the Send button waits.
- If sending fails, the page checks whether the PC session is still alive. If it is, the page resends once automatically, and if that fails too it shows "network error - please try again".
- If the PC session has ended, it shows "the connection to the PC is gone (closed or timed out) - reopen Mobile Drop on the PC and scan the QR code again".
- Recording directly in the page, without opening a recorder app, needs the HTTPS Cloudflare tunnel.

If the page will not open on the phone

- Check that both devices are on the same Wi-Fi. Guest networks and some routers stop devices from talking to each other ("AP isolation"). A VPN on the PC or the phone can also get in the way.
- On Windows you may see a firewall prompt for syki::sok the first time. Allow it on private networks.
- The QR code uses the address of the network adapter that carries your default route (virtual adapters such as WSL or Docker are skipped). If your phone is not on that network, use the Cloudflare connection above.

The toolbar icon can be hidden or moved under Settings → General → Toolbar & right-click menu. The shortcut and the Command Palette entry work either way.

---

### Cloudflare Mobile Bridge — Send From Your Phone (works even while closed)

**In short:** Send notes, photos, and voice memos from a mobile PWA (Web App) to your self-hosted Cloudflare Workers + D1 backend, and syki::sok automatically appends them to today's scrap the next time it opens. Unlike Mobile Drop, you do not need to be on the same Wi-Fi, and your PC does not need to be on. Completely private and self-hosted on Cloudflare's free tier.

**Phone (PWA)**Send notes, photos, or voice recordings from browser or home-screen app

**Cloudflare Workers + D1**Dedicated Worker and DB store encrypted messages even when PC is off

**PC (syki::sok)**Polls periodically (default 30s), transcribes via Gemini/OCR, appends to today's scrap

**One-time setup**

1. **Deploy the Cloudflare Worker**In the `tools/cf-bridge` folder of the repository, run `npm run deploy` to deploy your personal Worker (`https://<worker-name>.workers.dev`) — completely free on Cloudflare's free tier
2. **Configure syki::sok**Open Settings → Sync → "Cloudflare Mobile Bridge", check Enable, and enter the Worker Endpoint URL and Auth Token
3. **Pair with your phone**Click "Show QR Code" in the settings dialog, scan it with your phone camera, and open the link. Add it to your home screen (PWA) to use it like a native app

**Using it**

1. **Open the PWA on your phone**Launch it from the home screen icon. Even offline, you can review recent submission history
2. **Enter text, capture photo, or record voice**Tap the camera icon for instant capture, or the mic icon for 1-tap voice recording. The history panel lets you delete items or purge with a 2-step safety lock
3. **Wait for it to land in syki::sok**If the PC is running, it arrives within the poll interval (default 30s); if closed, everything is fetched and transcribed on next launch under `## Mobile [14:20:05]` in `scraps/YYYY-MM-DD.md`

| Sent from Phone | What lands in the scrap |
| --- | --- |
| Photo / Image | Transcribed into Markdown text by the Gemini vision model. If unset or failed, saved under `assets/` and linked. |
| Voice memo / recording | Automatically transcribed into natural text by Gemini audio model (`gemini-3.5-transcribe`). |
| Text / URL | Appended as plain text; bare URLs become Markdown links automatically. |

---

### Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P)

**In one line:** Search and run syki::sok's commands and the notes in the folder you opened, using only the keyboard. Ctrl + Shift + P No setup needed
Ctrl + Shift + P: the command palette

1. **Input field** Type to filter commands and notes
2. **Highlighted command** Press Enter to run it
3. **Description and shortcut** Each command shows a one-line description and its assigned key

1. **Open the palette**Ctrl + Shift + P (macOS: Cmd + Shift + P)
2. **Type to filter**Type part of a command name or a note title (substring match)
3. **Choose and run**A command runs, and a note opens

Limits and details

- It searches the commands and the notes in the workspace folder you have opened.
- The AI and command entries are "Ask AI", "Command Bar" (opens in the mode you used last), "Command Bar: Run a Command" and "Command Bar: AI Writes the Command". The last two have no key by default.
- "Insert task snippet" opens the list of ready-made LLM, agent and command tasks at the caret. Insert one, then press Ctrl + Enter to run it (see Auto Selector).
- "Quick Capture" (Windows only) opens the small note popup (see Quick Capture). "Open inbox folder" (Windows and macOS) shows the folder the hot folder watches, and is listed only while the hot folder is on.
- Type "tag" for "Add a tag to this entry", "Add a tag to the whole note" and "Remove a tag" (see Add and Remove Tags). They act on the note in the editor you were working in.
- "Open the lessons file" opens the rules you saved for an agent as an ordinary tab, to edit (it asks which agent when several have one; see Lessons).
- "About syki::sok" opens the version, license, folders and links (see About syki::sok). "Help and manual (web)" opens the online manual at once.
- Matching is a plain substring match, not a fuzzy search.
- With two panes open, a command runs on the pane you were working in (left or right), and closing the palette gives the focus back to that pane.
- Settings are not searchable. Open the settings screen with Ctrl + , (macOS: Cmd + ,).

---

### About syki::sok, Updates and Where Your Text Goes

**In one line:** The Help (**?**) button opens a small menu with the online manual and **About syki::sok**: the version, the license, the folders that hold your settings and notes, links, and a button that copies the details for a bug report. The Ask and Rewrite bars say where your text is going, and ask once before it goes to a cloud service.
About syki::sok

1. **Version** The version, the operating system, and the build it was made from
2. **Updates** Whether a newer release exists. Check now asks GitHub at once, whatever the start-up setting says
3. **Folders** Where your settings and daily notes are kept. Open shows the folder in the file manager
4. **Copy details** Puts the version, OS, web view and folders on the clipboard, for a bug report

1. **Open it**Click the Help (**?**) button and choose **About syki::sok**, or open the Command Palette and type "About". A fresh installation hides the Help button from the toolbar; the palette always works
2. **Check for a new version**Press **Check now**. If a newer release exists, **Release notes** opens its page
3. **Report a problem**Press **Copy details** and paste the text into your report. It holds the version, the operating system, the web view and the folder names, always in English. No note text and no keys. The folder names can contain your user name

The Help menu when a newer version is known

1. **The notice** The newer version and the one you have
2. **Release notes** Opens the page of that version
3. **About syki::sok** Opens the dialog above

Limits and details

- **The Help menu:** the online manual and About syki::sok. When a newer version is known, it starts with a notice that states the version and has a **Release notes** button; opening the menu also clears the small dot on the Help button for that version. The palette entry "Help and manual (web)" opens the manual at once.
- **No Help button on the toolbar:** a fresh installation hides it (see "A short toolbar to start with"), so the dot has nowhere to sit. syki::sok then shows a message once when it finds a newer version, and About syki::sok (from the palette) always shows the version and the Release notes button.
- **Signing:** About says how this build is signed. The macOS build is ad-hoc signed and not notarized by Apple, so macOS asks you to approve it the first time (see "macOS First Launch"). The Windows build is not code-signed, so Windows may show a warning the first time you run it.
- **Build:** a program built from a git checkout also shows its commit and build date, and the details text repeats them.
- **Open a folder:** a folder that syki::sok has not created yet (the daily notes folder before your first note) cannot be opened; the dialog says so under the row.

**The update check**

By default syki::sok asks GitHub, about 2.5 seconds after it starts, whether a newer release exists. It is one request to `api.github.com` for the number of the latest release; nothing from your notes or settings goes with it (GitHub sees the request as any web server does, including your IP address). If a newer version exists, a small dot appears on the Help button.

Settings → General → Updates & Privacy

1. **Check for updates at start-up** Off means no request at start-up. Check now in About syki::sok still works
2. **Allowed hosts** The cloud services the Ask and Rewrite bars, Deep search and Lessons may send text to (shown only after you allowed one)
3. **Forget** Clears the list; it takes effect when you press Save

- **Turn it off:** Settings → General → "Updates & Privacy" → "Check for updates at start-up". With it off, syki::sok makes no request at start-up. **Check now** in About syki::sok still works whenever you press it.
- **For administrators:** the switch is `general.checkUpdates` in `config.json` (Windows: `%APPDATA%\syki-sok\`; macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/syki-sok/`; About syki::sok shows the exact folder). `false` turns the start-up check off. A missing key, or any other value, leaves it on, so settings files from older versions keep today's behaviour. A file that holds only `{"general":{"checkUpdates":false}}` is enough, and the setting is part of the "General" section of an exported package, so one package can carry it to many PCs. Note that a PC that already has a settings file counts as an existing installation for the short first toolbar and the Welcome note.

**Where your text goes**

The Ask AI bar the first time it is used with a cloud model

1. **Where the text goes** The model and "(cloud)". A local model reads "Local Ollama (model)"
2. **The question** Shown once per host. Nothing is sent and the note is not touched until you answer
3. **Allow and send** Remembers the host. Cancel keeps your text and asks again next time

The Ask AI bar and the Rewrite bar show, in the row under the field, where the text will be sent: **Local Ollama (qwen2.5:latest)** for a model on this computer or your local network, or **gemini-flash-lite-latest (cloud)** for an online service. Hold the pointer over it to see the host name.

- **The first time for a cloud host:** the bar asks "Your text will be sent over the internet to <host>. Allow it?" with **Allow and send** and **Cancel**. Nothing is sent, and the note is not touched, until you answer. **Allow and send** remembers that host (`general.cloudConsent` in `config.json`); **Cancel** keeps your text in the bar and asks again next time.
- **A local model is never asked** (Ollama, or any server on this computer or your local network).
- **The answer stays on this PC:** the allowed hosts are saved with your settings on this PC only. An exported package does not carry them and an imported package does not change them.
- **Forget:** Settings → General → "Updates & Privacy" lists the allowed hosts, with a **Forget** button that takes effect when you press Save.
- **Only these two bars, Deep search and Lessons ask.** The other features that use a model (text prediction, proofreading, Suggestions, tasks, voice input, image OCR) use their own settings in Settings → AI Models and are not asked about. The AI label in the status bar tells local from cloud. A bar that only collects an instruction for a task (Ctrl + Enter on a plain sentence) shows no destination, because the task decides.

**The operation-rhythm log (off by default)**

Settings → General → "Updates & Privacy" → **Keep an operation-rhythm log**. It is **off** until you turn it on; while it is off, syki::sok does not even listen for key presses or the mouse. When it is on, every 30 seconds (only if something happened) one line of numbers about how you work is written to a file on this PC:

- **Typing:** how many key presses, how long a key is held, the interval between presses and how even it is, how often you press Backspace / Delete and the arrow keys, how many pauses of 2 seconds or more. Presses made while an IME is composing (Japanese input) are counted apart, because a Backspace there edits the reading, not the text.
- **Mouse and scrolling:** how far the pointer moved, how often it turned sharply, how many wheel events, how often the scroll direction reversed, how far you scrolled.
- **Commands:** how many times you opened the Ask, Rewrite or Command bar or Quick Actions, which one was last (a number), and how soon after your last key press.
- **Voice input:** how many times it was started and for how long the microphone was on. Nothing about the audio or what was said.
- **The window:** whether it is floating, maximized, snapped to one side of the screen (Win+←/→) or full screen; whether Zen mode is on; editor, preview or split view; whether that changed since the last line. Not its position or size. And how many times it lost the focus and for how long it had it: that shows when you work next to other apps.

**What is never kept:** what you type, which keys you press, where the pointer is or where you click, where the window is on the screen or how big it is, which other app you used, the contents of any note, and any audio. Every field is a number; the program that writes the file refuses a line that holds anything else. Only the editors and the inputs of the AI bars are watched (not the fields in Settings).

- **Where:** a file per day, `YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl`, in the `telemetry` folder next to `config.json` (Windows: `%APPDATA%\syki-sok\telemetry\`). It is not in your notes folder, so it is not synced with git. Nothing is ever sent over the network.
- **How long:** files older than 30 days are deleted automatically. **Delete all logs** in the same place removes them at once, and **Open the folder** shows them.
- **For administrators:** the switch is `general.telemetry` in `config.json` (true = on; missing or anything else = off). It belongs to this PC: it is not in a settings package (.sykipack) and an import does not switch it on.

**The activity log (off by default, two switches)**

Next to the operation-rhythm log, Settings → General → "Updates & Privacy" has two more switches. Both are **off** until you turn them on. They exist so that a **local** model can tell you where you left off ("what did I work on this morning?") without any of it leaving the PC.

- **Keep a log of notes and requests:** which note you wrote in and how many characters it grew or shrank by (a line per 30 seconds of writing), and each request you typed in the Ask or Rewrite bar: the words you typed, whether the model is local or in the cloud, and what became of it (put in the note, failed, cancelled). Never the text of your notes (the note is on disk already) and never which keys you pressed.
- **Also keep which app is in front (Windows):** every 2 seconds syki::sok asks Windows for the window in front and writes down the program's name and the window's title when it changes. Password managers (KeePass, 1Password, Bitwarden, LastPass and similar) and private browsing windows are left out, and syki's own window has no title. Add more words in `config.json`: `general.activityExclude`.

**How it looks to security software:** the front window is read with plain calls (`GetForegroundWindow`, the window title, the program's name). There is no hook of any kind, no reading of key or mouse state, no raw input, no screen capture, no clipboard watching, and no other process is touched beyond asking its name. The same goes for the rhythm log, which only uses the events the page itself receives. A test keeps the list of calls this code may never make.

- **Where:** a file per day in the `activity` folder next to `config.json` (Windows: `%APPDATA%\syki-sok\activity\`), never in your notes folder, so it is not synced with git. Nothing is sent over the network. Files older than 30 days are deleted; **Delete the activity log** removes them at once.
- **Cloud models:** the log is handed to a local model. It is given to a cloud model only for a request you approved, after being shown what would be sent.
- **For administrators:** `general.activityEdits` and `general.activityApps` in `config.json` (true = on; anything else = off), and `general.activityExclude` (an array of words for programs to leave out). All belong to this PC: they are not in a settings package (.sykipack) and an import does not switch them on.

**Meaning search, Deep search, Lessons and printing**

These work as follows. See Meaning Search, Deep Search, Lessons and Print or Save as PDF.

- **Meaning search** (experimental, off by default): the text of your notes goes to the embedding model set in `semantic.model` when the index is built or updated (`syki scrap index`), and the text you search for goes to the same model. By default that is a model on this PC (Ollama). A cloud host is used only after you have allowed it (`semantic.privacy.cloudConsent` in `config.json`). The index stays on this PC, outside the scraps folder, and is never Git-synced.
- **Deep search:** excerpts of the notes it found go to the Text LLM, and only when you press **Run** in its confirmation dialog, which first shows what goes and where. With a filter on, it uses only what the filtered list shows: nothing outside the filter is sent, not even an entry next to a short one that was found. A key, token or password in an excerpt is blanked out before sending. A model that is not on this PC (a machine on your local network included) needs your consent once per host, and **Allow and run** remembers it in the same list as the Ask bar (**Forget** is in Settings → General → "Updates & Privacy").
- **Lessons:** when you press **Create a proposal** in the Lessons dialog, a cut-down record of that one agent run goes to the Text LLM: the start of the instruction, the end of the agent's output, the error message and your note in the dialog (at most 6,800 characters of it). The rest of your notes does not go. A key, token or password in it is blanked out before sending, and the dialog first shows how many characters go and where. A model that is not on this PC needs your consent once per host, in the same list as the Ask bar, and syki::sok checks it again before it sends. Saved rules stay in a file in the settings folder on this PC, outside the scraps folder, so Git sync does not carry them and an exported settings package does not hold them. They go to a model only as part of an agent's instruction, when that agent runs.
- **Printing and saving a PDF** keep everything on this PC.

---

## 03 Settings Reference

**In one line:** The settings screen has five tabs: General, AI Models, Agent, Sync and Shortcuts. Open it with the slider icon in the header, or with "Settings..." in the right-click menu.
Settings: the General tab (theme, window and editor behavior)

1. **Theme** The accent color scheme
2. **Language** The interface language: English or Japanese
3. **Startup and window** Restore tabs and unsaved notes, start in split view, stay in the tray
4. **Editor and typing** Autosave, IME Guardian, AI proofreading, cursor light. The toolbar and right-click menu are set further down this tab (see the steps below)

**Basic and advanced view:** the sections most people never need (Ghost Text, image OCR, voice input, image generation, commands, the Auto selector, Quick Actions, Cloudflare Mobile Bridge and the hot folder) start folded. Click a section title to open it, or tick **Show advanced** at the top right of the dialog to open them all (the choice is remembered). The explanation under a field sits behind the small **?** button next to it. Nothing is removed: a folded section still saves its values.

### 1. General Tab

| Setting | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base Look | Ink | Choose between Ink (dark classic background `#1e1e1e`) and Paper (light washi tone `#fbfbf9`). Native window frame and title bar adapt accordingly. |
| Accent color | Dark Olive | Dark Olive, Classic Blue, Forest Teal, Charcoal Monochrome, Vermilion, or a custom color chosen with the color picker or HEX code. |
| Bar transparency | Glass | Choose how the header and status bar blend with the background: Light, Solid, or Glass (backdrop blur). |
| Auto-hide bars | Enabled (ON) | Header and status bar automatically fade out when you type or scroll to keep you in flow, and restore on mouse movement. |
| Split boundary | Dots | Appearance of the divider in two-page view: Dots (gutter stipple), Shade (shadow only), or Line (1px hairline). Can be adjusted with keyboard via F6. |
| Editor font | Default (monospace) | Specify any monospace or proportional font family installed on your OS (e.g. Cascadia Code, Consolas, Fira Code). |
| Diagram (Mermaid) colors | Dark | Dark, Light, Gray or Green. The last three draw diagrams on a white card, which helps when a diagram is hard to read on the dark preview. The button on each diagram in the preview switches dark and light. |
| Language | English / Japanese | Switch the UI language. |
| Restore Open Tabs | Enabled | Restores unsaved buffers and previous tabs upon application launch. |
| 2-Pane Split by Default | Disabled | Always launches in split view when checked. |
| Resident in Tray | Enabled (Windows) | On Windows, the close button keeps syki::sok in the tray instead of quitting, and Ctrl+Alt+M brings it back in milliseconds. macOS has no tray: closing the window always keeps syki::sok in the Dock, and this checkbox is disabled there with the hint "Not available on this platform yet; this setting currently has no effect." |
| Check for updates at start-up | Enabled | About 2.5 seconds after start-up, asks `api.github.com` for the number of the latest release (nothing else is sent) and shows a dot on the Help button when a newer one exists. Off means no request at start-up. **Check now** in About syki::sok works either way. Stored as `general.checkUpdates`. See About syki::sok. |
| Keep an operation-rhythm log | Disabled | Every 30 seconds, writes numbers about how you work (key rhythm, mouse and scroll, which AI bars you opened, voice input started and for how long) to a file on this PC. Never what you type, which keys, where you click or any audio; kept 30 days. While off, nothing is watched. See the operation-rhythm log. |
| Keep a log of notes and requests | Disabled | Writes down which note you wrote in and how much it changed, and the requests you typed in the Ask and Rewrite bars with what became of them. Never the text of your notes or the keys you pressed. Kept 30 days on this PC for a local model. See the activity log. |
| Also keep which app is in front | Disabled (Windows) | Every 2 seconds, writes down the program's name and window title of the window in front when it changes. Password managers and private windows are left out. No hooks, no key or mouse state, no screen, no clipboard. |
| Cloud AI hosts you have allowed | None | Listed only after the Ask or Rewrite bar (or Deep search, or the Lessons dialog) has asked about a cloud host and you allowed it. **Forget** clears the list when you press Save. Stored as `general.cloudConsent` on this PC only (never exported). |
| Autosave on 1.5s Pause | Enabled | Silently saves existing files upon a 1.5-second typing pause. If another program (another editor, a Git pull, a sync client) changed the file after you opened or last saved it, nothing is written: the tab shows a red "!", autosave pauses for that note, and Ctrl + S asks whether to save under another name, load the file (your own text is kept in a new tab), or overwrite it. A note with nothing unsaved simply shows the new text. A file that uses CRLF line endings keeps them when you save. |
| IME Guardian | Enabled only if the system language is Japanese (Disabled by default on macOS) | Protects code blocks against IME full-width character leakage. On macOS the OS input source cannot be switched automatically yet, so it starts off there and Settings shows a hint saying so. |
| Enable AI typo & error correction (Alt+C) | Enabled | Turns the Alt + C proofreading command on or off. |
| Subtle cursor light on idle | Enabled | Shows a soft glow around the caret when typing stops. |
| Ctrl+V turns web, Word and Excel content into Markdown | Enabled | Converts only HTML with structure (tables, headings, lists, links) to Markdown; code and logs are pasted as they are. Ctrl + Shift + V always pastes as it is. When off, Ctrl + V pastes plain text and Ctrl + Shift + V converts. |
| Toggle comment writes | One comment per line | What Ctrl + / writes: one `<!-- -->` per line, or one comment around the selected lines. See Comment Out Lines. |
| Toolbar & right-click menu | Everything shown | Show, hide and reorder the toolbar icons and right-click menu items. See "Adjusting the toolbar and right-click menu" below for the steps. |

**Adjusting the toolbar and right-click menu**

1. **Open the section**In Settings → General, open the "Toolbar & right-click menu" section (click its title; it folds like the other sections)
2. **Choose what to show**Tick the toolbar icons and right-click items you want. Use the arrows to reorder them within their group
3. **Changes apply at once**"Cancel" undoes them. "Reset to default" shows every icon again in the original order (a fresh installation starts with a shorter toolbar, so this is also the way to get the full one)

The Toolbar & right-click menu section opened

1. **Section title** Click to open or fold it, like every other section
2. **Checkboxes** Tick to show, clear to hide (only the Settings icon always stays)
3. **Up and down arrows** Move an item within its group

The menu you get by right-clicking a selected line

1. **Editing commands** Undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, select all
2. **Open Notes** Expands a submenu listing all open tabs with active (checked) and unsaved marks for instant switching
3. **Navigation** Find, replace, go to line, command palette, open folder
4. **AI and command bar** Ask AI, proofread, Command Bar, voice input
5. **View commands** Preview and open to the side (scroll the menu for Zen mode and full screen). Which items are shown can be changed in Settings

- The Settings icon can be reordered but not hidden (it always stays, so you can get back to the settings screen).
- Items you hide can still be used with their shortcuts and from the command palette.

The **Export...** and **Import...** buttons at the bottom of the Settings dialog carry your settings, agent definitions and skills to another PC in one package (`.sykipack`). Details: 6. Export and Import Settings (Packages).

---

### 2. AI Models Tab

**In one line:** From a fully offline local LLM to the latest cloud APIs, you can choose a model for each feature.
Settings: the AI Models tab (scrolled to the Voice input group)

1. **Voice model** The model used for transcription
2. **API style** "Auto" picks the API from the model name, or you can force one
3. **Language codes** Comma-separated. Empty means auto-detect
4. **Mode** Smart tidies the text, and Verbatim keeps every word
5. **Custom vocabulary** Names and jargon, one per line
6. **Silence timeout** How many seconds of silence stop the recording automatically

- **Feature → Which model setting it uses:** the card at the top of the tab, showing which setting each feature reads. For example, Write (Ask AI) and Chat use the Text LLM, Ghost Text and Image OCR have their own settings, and Suggestions (Quick Actions) are configured on the Agent tab.
- **Local AI (Ollama):** a status badge with **Start** and **Stop** buttons for Ollama, plus **Install Gemma 4**, which installs Ollama if it is missing and pulls the `gemma4:e2b` model.
- **Writing & commands:** Base URL, model name, API key, and System Prompt. The protocol is detected from the URL and shown beneath it: Ollama, Gemini-compatible, or OpenAI-compatible.
- **Inline Autocomplete (Ghost Text):** its own URL, model, and key, plus the suggestion delay (default 500 ms; the settings screen allows 200–2000, but the effective minimum is 300 ms) and the maximum prediction tokens (default 30, range 10–100).
- **Image analysis (OCR):** the vision model and key, such as Gemini Flash Lite or Qwen 2.5 VL, plus a toggle "Automatically transcribe pasted images (Ctrl+V) using Gemini OCR" (on by default). When the toggle is off, or there is no API key, a pasted image is saved to assets and linked instead (like Ctrl+Shift+V). Pictures from the hot folder, Screen Capture and Send To are read with these settings too.
- **Image generation:** the model, aspect ratio, and resolution used by "Render Image...". If its Gemini API key is blank, it inherits the Vision key and then the Text key, in that order.
- **Voice input:** Right below the Image analysis (OCR) settings. For how to use it, see Voice Input. The settings are listed in the table below.
- **Realtime and Batch (Voice input group):** each block has an **Engine**: "Gemini (cloud)" (the default) or "Whisper (on this PC, offline)" (Windows x64 only), its own Gemini model and API style, and its own Whisper model. Realtime is voice input and dropped audio files; Batch is the meeting recording, Mobile Drop, the hot folder and Cloudflare Mobile Bridge. The Whisper program and options are in the group "Whisper (on this PC)". The settings are in the second table below, and the download steps are under On-device Whisper.

**Voice input settings**

| Setting | Config file key | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Voice model | `voice.model` | `gemini-3.5-transcribe` | Suggestions: `gemini-3.5-transcribe`, `gemini-flash-lite-latest`. `gemini-3.5-transcribe-live` (the streaming variant) cannot be used for recorded audio, and choosing it causes an error. |
| API style | `voice.apiStyle` | Auto (`auto`) | Auto / Interactions API / generateContent. Auto uses the Interactions API when the model name contains "transcribe", and generateContent otherwise. |
| Language codes | `voice.languageCodes` | Empty | Comma-separated BCP-47 codes (for example `ja-JP, en-US`). Empty means auto-detect, which also handles mixed languages. Used only with the Interactions API. |
| Mode | `voice.mode` | Smart (`smart`) | Smart removes fillers and formats the text for reading. Verbatim (`verbatim`) transcribes word for word. Used only with the Interactions API. |
| Custom vocabulary | `voice.customVocabulary` | Empty | One term per line (names, jargon). Up to 1000 terms, but about 100 works best. The Interactions API takes it as a spelling hint; the on-device Whisper takes the first terms (up to 200 characters) after its own initial prompt. |
| Silence timeout (s) | `voice.silence_timeout_sec` | 5 | 1–30. Recording stops by itself after this many seconds of silence. |
| Transcription prompt | `voice.prompt` | Built-in instruction | Used only by generateContent-style models. |
| API key / Base URL | `voice.apiKey` / `voice.baseUrl` | Empty | If empty, the Image analysis (OCR) key and Base URL are used. The settings screen has no separate fields for them, so a separate key is possible only by writing it in the config file directly. |

**Speech engine settings** (the blocks Realtime and Batch of the Voice input group, and the group "Whisper (on this PC)"; `<profile>` is `realtime` or `batch`)

| Setting | Config file key | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Engine | `voice.realtime.engine`, `voice.batch.engine` | Gemini (cloud) (`gemini`) | "Gemini (cloud)" or "Whisper (on this PC, offline)" (`whisper-local`). One for each kind: Realtime (voice input, dropped audio files) and Batch (meeting recording, Mobile Drop, hot folder, Cloudflare Mobile Bridge). With Whisper as the Realtime engine the tidy-up second stage is off and speaking over a selection is refused. Whisper is for Windows x64 only; on macOS the settings say so. |
| Whisper program, Model | `voice.<profile>.whisper.model` | kotoba-whisper v2.0 quantized | Two parts downloaded on demand, each with Download, Remove and Cancel and a progress display: the Whisper program (about 9 MB) and a model. Stored under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\syki-sok\components`. See On-device Whisper for the model list. |
| Model file (ggml .bin) | `voice.<profile>.whisper.modelPath` | Empty | Used with "Custom: a model file on this PC". |
| Model URL (https), SHA-256 (optional) | `voice.<profile>.whisper.customUrl`, `voice.<profile>.whisper.customSha256` | Empty | Used with "Custom: download from a URL". The download is verified against the SHA-256 when you enter one. |
| Language | `voice.<profile>.whisper.language` | Empty (auto-detect) | Examples: `ja`, `en`. |
| Threads (0 = auto) | `voice.<profile>.whisper.threads` | 0 | How many processor threads Whisper may use. 0 lets it choose. |
| Initial prompt | `voice.<profile>.whisper.prompt` | Empty | Names or terms to bias recognition toward. |
| If Whisper fails, retry with Gemini (sends the audio out) | `voice.<profile>.whisper.cloudFallback` | Off | Turn it on to fall back to Gemini when Whisper fails or is not installed. The audio then leaves your PC. |

---

### 3. Agent & CLI Tab

**In one line:** Following the three verbs, this tab has four groups: "Commands (Run)", "Agents (Request)", "Auto selector (Let it decide)" and "Suggestions (Quick Actions)". On Windows, a fifth group at the end, "OS Integration (Send To)", adds an entry to the Explorer Send To menu.
Settings: the Agent tab (scrolled to the Agents (Request) settings)

1. **Open agents.yaml** Opens the file that defines agents and notations
2. **Agent** The default agent, with a badge that shows whether its command is installed
3. **Agent timeout** Seconds before a run is cut off
4. **Change highlight duration (Ghost Diff)** In milliseconds
5. **Live output preview (Hover Peek)** Shows the agent's latest output in the task panel

**Commands (Run)**: settings for the command bar.

- **CLI Model Name:** the model that writes commands in the Command Bar's AI mode (Ctrl+E, then Tab). Leave it blank to inherit the AI Models tab.
- **Where the command's output goes:** The default is "Below the selected text (the selection stays)": the output goes below the selection's last line, unless it is the same text the command ran on (then nothing is added). "Over the selected text (like a filter)" replaces the selection with the output, as before.
- **Open CLI execution results in a new tab:** When on (the default), the output is put into the note as set above and the result also opens in a new tab (with no selection, only the new tab opens). When off, no new tab opens, and with no selection the output is added at the end of the note (with "Over the selected text", the whole note is replaced by the output).
- **Max Stdin Pipe Size (MB):** Changing this has no effect. The limit for `cat log | syki` is fixed at 10 MB, to keep a huge file from spiking memory.

**Agents (Request)**: settings for the agents your slots call.

- **Open agents.yaml:** opens the file that defines notations, agents (with their aliases), recipes and your own snippets. A commented template is generated if none exists yet; it explains `@name`, `aliases`, `snippets` and how to switch an agent off (`enabled`, `disabled_agents`).
- **Agent:** the default agent used when a notation does not name one. The Auto selector also uses it when a line looks like a job for an agent. The list is built from the `agents.yaml` currently loaded: each entry reads `key - description` (just the key when there is no description), agents you switched off are not listed, and a line under the list names them (for example "Disabled in agents.yaml: agy, hermes"). Below it, a warning appears when the selected agent skips its permission prompts, and a box **Agent definitions to review** lists agents in your agents.yaml that still copy a replaced built-in definition or would run your instruction as a shell command, with **Copy the new definition** and **Hide until this list changes** (see Delegate).
- **Agent timeout (seconds):** how long a run may take before it is cut off (default 180 s, range 10–600 s). If an `agents.yaml` already exists (even one created by "Open agents.yaml"), the file's value wins and this field is not used.
- **Ghost Diff highlight time:** how long the amber line shows on the left edge of the editor right after a result lands (default 4000 ms, range 1000–10000). You can undo with Esc during that time and for 1 second after it. The settings screen labels it "Change highlight duration (ms) (Ghost Diff)".
- **Hover Peek:** shows the agent's latest output line in the task panel.

**Auto selector (Let it decide)**: settings for the Auto selector. This group sits between "Agents (Request)" and "Suggestions (Quick Actions)".

Settings: the Agent tab, scrolled to the Auto selector group

1. **Auto selector group** Between Agents (Request) and Suggestions (Quick Actions)
2. **Let Ctrl+Enter decide** On by default. When off, Ctrl+Enter only runs `{{ }}` slots, as before
3. **Confirm before an auto-detected agent or command runs** On by default. The line is rewritten first, and a second Ctrl+Enter runs it

- **Let Ctrl+Enter decide: ask the AI, hand over to an agent, or run a command:** on by default (config key `autoSelector.enabled`). When off, Ctrl+Enter only runs `{{ }}` slots, as before. A task you wrote yourself (`[[ @llm ... ]]`, `[[ $ ... ]]`, `{{ @agent ... }}`) still runs with Ctrl+Enter; only the guessing stops.
- **Confirm before an auto-detected agent or command runs:** on by default (`autoSelector.agentConfirm`). The line is rewritten first; press Ctrl+Enter again to run it (Ctrl+Z undoes the rewrite). When off, an agent or a command runs right after the rewrite (an agent that acts without asking is still confirmed first, before the line is rewritten). An AI instruction always runs at once.
- Both settings travel with the "Agent & Quick Actions" section of a settings package. A config that has no such group gets the defaults (both on).

**Suggestions (Quick Actions)**: settings for Quick Actions (Ctrl+J).

- **Suggest actions automatically while typing:** whether cards appear on their own after a pause.
- **Manual trigger only (suppress auto-popup, press Ctrl+J):** turn off automatic suggestions and show cards only when you press Ctrl+J.
- **Quick Actions delay (seconds):** how long a pause has to be before cards appear.
- **API Base URL / Model Name / API Key:** where Jev (or another model) is reached for the candidates. Leave the API Key empty and the Base URL at its default (`https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`, model `jev-latest`) to use the built-in local rules; nothing is sent until you enter a key or change the URL. With an OpenRouter key, keep the defaults; with a TypeSafe key, set the Base URL to `https://api.typesafe.ai`. Details are under "data that is sent" in Quick Actions.

**OS Integration (Send To)** (Windows only): the last group on the tab.

- **Send To menu (image → OCR):** A badge shows "Installed" or "Not installed". **Add** puts **syki::sok (OCR)** in Explorer's Send To menu, and **Remove** takes it out again. Right-click an image → Send to → syki::sok (OCR), and its text is appended to today's scrap with no window opening. The steps and the matching `syki ocr` command are under Send To menu and the ocr command.

---

### 4. Sync Tab (Git & Scraps)

**In one line:** Set the folder where daily scraps are saved, and background auto-sync to GitHub.
Settings: the Sync tab (scraps folder and Git)

1. **Daily scraps folder** The folder where scraps are saved
2. **Background Git sync** Switch it on or off
3. **Git remote URL** The URL of the scraps repository
4. **Link / Init** Connects the folder to the remote
5. **Repository status badge** Shows the current Git state

- **Daily Scraps Folder:** Path where `cat file | syki` and daily notes reside. Use **Browse...** to pick it. You can point it directly to Google Drive for desktop (e.g. `G:\My Drive\...`) or Dropbox to synchronize scraps across multiple PCs. When using Google Drive, right-click the folder and choose "Available offline" so notes remain instantly readable and writable without an internet connection, automatically syncing upon reconnecting. Furthermore, historical scraps (`scraps/`) can be automatically distilled into structured topic notes (`wiki/`) and an index (`INDEX.md`) via the included `tools/absorb-scraps.ps1` / `.sh` scripts or the agent skill (`skills/syki`), moving processed logs to `archive/` for a Zero-Inbox knowledge compilation workflow.
- **Enable background Git sync:** Runs `git pull --rebase` on launch, then runs `git add/commit/push` in the background once you stop editing. It works when the scraps folder is a Git repository. A remote is not required, but without one the push fails.
- **Git Auto-Push Debounce (seconds):** How long to wait after the last edit before pushing (default 30, range 5–3600).
- **Remote Branch:** The branch to sync with (default `main`).
- **Git Remote URL, Test Connection, and Link / Init:** Enter the URL of an empty GitHub repository (`https://github.com/user/scraps.git`), click **Test Connection** to check access, then click **Link / Init**. It runs `git init` if needed, sets `origin`, makes an initial commit, and pushes with `push -u`.
- **Cloudflare Mobile Bridge:** further down the same tab. Configure your self-hosted Cloudflare Worker Endpoint URL and Auth Token, and scan the QR code to pair with your phone immediately. See Cloudflare Mobile Bridge.
- **Hot folder:** the last section of this tab. Tick "Watch a folder: images are OCR'd, audio is transcribed, both appended to today's scrap" (off by default; config key `inbox.enabled`) and set "Watched Folder Path:" with **Browse...** (default `~/Documents/syki-sok/inbox`; `inbox.dir`). Processed files are moved into the `assets` folder next to your scraps and never deleted. See Hot Folder.
- **Keep images on this PC: read them with the on-device OCR only (less accurate):** in the same section, off by default (config key `vision.ocrMode`: empty, or `"on-device"`). When on, images are never sent to the vision model. It applies to the hot folder, Screen Capture, the Send To entry and the `ocr` command, but not to pasting with Ctrl + V. Windows only: the checkbox is hidden on macOS, which has no on-device OCR engine.

Caution: everything in the scraps folder gets committed

Git sync runs `git add .`, commit and push in the scraps folder. An `.env` or `.syki-sok/agents.yaml` kept there is committed too, so do not keep secrets in that folder.

---

### 5. Shortcut Cheatsheet

**In one line:** You can reassign most keys in Settings → Shortcuts. Click a row's key button and press the new combination.

| Action | Windows | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Global Summon (bring to front; it does not hide the window)** | Ctrl + Alt + M | Option + Cmd + M |
| **High-Speed Scrap Search** | Ctrl + Shift + F | Cmd + Shift + F |
| **Command Palette** | Ctrl + Shift + P | Cmd + Shift + P |
| **Ask AI** | Ctrl + L | Cmd + L |
| **AI Proofreading & Correction** | Alt + C | Cmd + Shift + C |
| **Suggest Quick Actions** | Ctrl + J | Cmd + J |
| **Command Bar (opens in the mode you used last)** | Ctrl + E | Cmd + E |
| **Mobile Drop (send from your phone via QR)** | Ctrl + Shift + U | Cmd + Shift + U |
| **Auto selector / run a slot (fixed key)** | Ctrl + Enter | Cmd + Enter |
| **Toggle Task Panel** | Alt + T | Option + T |
| **Split Editor Right** | Ctrl + \ | Cmd + \ |
| **Preview to the Side** | Ctrl + Alt + V | Cmd + Option + V |
| **Move the divider between two pages** (reach it with F6; Shift = 10 points, Home / End = narrowest / widest, Enter = half and half) | ← → | ← → |
| **Paste as it is (plain text; images saved as files)** | Ctrl + Shift + V | Cmd + Shift + V |
| **Voice Input** | Ctrl + Shift + R | Cmd + Shift + R |
| **Quick Capture (global, opens the note popup)** | Ctrl + Shift + Q | Not available (Windows only) |
| **Open Link** | Ctrl + Click | Cmd + Click |
| **Reveal Link (Explorer / Finder)** | Alt + Click | Option + Click |
| **Zen Mode** | Shift + F11 | Ctrl + Cmd + Z |
| **Go round the note, the header, the tabs, the divider between two pages and the status bar** | F6 | F6 |
| **Full Screen** | F11 | Ctrl + Cmd + F |
| **Accept Ghost Text (Word)** | Ctrl + → | Option + → |
| **Insert Date / Time** | F5 | Cmd + Shift + I |
| **Toggle Comment (hide the lines in <!-- -->)** | Ctrl + / | Cmd + / |

The keys "Command Bar: CLI mode" and "Command Bar: AI mode" have no default key, and you can assign them here. Ctrl + K is not used by default either, so it is free to assign.

The "Quick Capture" row exists on Windows only. It is a global key: it works from any program, not just inside syki::sok. Clear the key and it is turned off. If another program already uses the combination, the change is refused with a message and the previous key stays. See Quick Capture.

**Reassigning a shortcut** (Settings → Shortcuts)

1. **Assign**Click the key button for a row, then press the combination you want. While it records, the hint reads "Press keys to set · Backspace to clear · Esc to cancel"
2. **If it is already used**A confirmation appears: "Already assigned to "<action>". Overwrite?" Choose "OK" (Enter) to move it (the other action becomes "Not Set"). "Cancel" or Esc changes nothing
3. **To leave it unassigned**While recording, press Backspace (or Delete) and the action becomes "Not Set" and does nothing. Esc cancels the recording. "Reset to Defaults" restores every default key

When checking for duplicates, Ctrl and Cmd are treated as the same key.

Settings: the Shortcuts tab. One row is waiting for a new key

1. **Hint line** Press the new keys. Backspace clears and Esc cancels
2. **Row being recorded** The button shows "Press key..." until you press a key combination
3. **Reset to Defaults** Puts every key back to its default

The overwrite confirmation when the recorded key is already assigned

1. **Confirmation message** It names the action that already uses the key, here "Suggest Quick Actions", and asks whether to overwrite it
2. **OK / Cancel** "OK" (Enter) overwrites, and "Cancel" (Esc) keeps the current assignment
3. **The action being reassigned** Here, Ask AI. This row's button was in the recording state

**Reserved keys that cannot be assigned**

The app uses the combinations below itself. If you try to assign one, you get the message `"<combo>" is reserved by the app and can't be assigned.`

| Platform | Keys that cannot be assigned |
| --- | --- |
| **Windows / Linux** | Ctrl + Tab Ctrl + , Ctrl + Shift + V (paste as it is) Alt + T (task panel) Ctrl + → (accept a ghost-text word) Ctrl + Enter (also with Shift or Alt added; the Auto selector and slots) Ctrl + C Ctrl + V Ctrl + X Ctrl + A Ctrl + Z Ctrl + Shift + Z (redo) Ctrl + Y |
| **macOS** | Ctrl + Tab Cmd + , Cmd + Q Cmd + H Cmd + Option + H Cmd + M Cmd + Z Cmd + Shift + Z Cmd + X Cmd + C Cmd + V Cmd + A Cmd + Tab Cmd + Space Cmd + Shift + V Option + T Cmd + → Cmd + Enter (also with Shift or Option added) |

**Other fixed keys that are not in the settings list**

- Ctrl + Enter: The Auto selector's key (see Auto Selector). It runs the task or slot under the caret, or does what the current line asks for. Variants with Shift or Alt added are treated the same way. That is why the default for "Insert Line Below" is Shift + Enter (Shift + Alt + Enter for "Insert Line Above").
- Ctrl + Click / Alt + Click: Open a link (a file, a folder, or a web address in the browser) / show the link's location (files only).
- Inside the Quick Capture popup (Windows): Enter sends, Ctrl + Enter is AI Send, Ctrl + Shift + Enter starts a screen capture and Esc closes it. See Quick Capture.
- Esc: Discards a voice recording.
- Paste as it is (Ctrl + Shift + V) is fixed and cannot be changed. The voice input key can be changed.

On macOS, use the corresponding keys from the table above.

---

### 6. Export and Import Settings (Packages)

**In one line:** Put your settings, agent definitions and skills into one `.sykipack` file and carry it to another PC. Use **Export...** and **Import...** at the bottom of the Settings dialog. API keys are left out at first

**Export** (Settings → Export...)

The top of "Export package": choose the format and the settings sections

1. **Format** A package (.sykipack), or a plain JSON file with the settings only
2. **Settings** Tick one box per section; All and None (top right) switch them all at once
3. **Sync** Marked "this PC only" and unticked at first, because the scrap folder path and similar values differ from PC to PC

The same dialog scrolled to the bottom: agent definitions, skills and options

1. **Agent definitions** The app-wide and the project agents file, with their paths; ticked at first
2. **Skills** Only the skills of the current project, grouped by folder; none are ticked at first
3. **Include API keys** Off at first; if you turn it on, anyone who gets the file can use your keys
4. **Export** Asks where to save the package

1. **Click "Export..."**At the bottom left of the Settings dialog; "Export package" opens
2. **Choose what goes in**Tick settings sections, agent definitions and skills; Sync and the skills start unticked
3. **Leave "Include API keys" off**So the file you hand over carries no keys; turn it on only to move to your own other PC
4. **Click "Export"**Pick where to save; `syki-sok-YYYYMMDD.sykipack` is written and a summary is shown

**Import** (Settings → Import...)

The contents of the chosen package (top part): choose what to import

1. **The package** File name, creation date and the syki::sok version that wrote it
2. **API key notice** "API keys are not included" means your current keys stay as they are; a package with keys shows a warning instead
3. **Settings** Only the sections the package holds; tick what you want to apply

The same dialog scrolled to the bottom: look for the "will overwrite" badges

1. **Will overwrite** Something with the same name already exists and will be replaced (it is backed up first)
2. **Skills warning** Skills are instructions an agent will follow; import only skills from sources you trust
3. **Backup note** Agent definitions and skills that would be overwritten are backed up first
4. **Import** Applies only what is ticked

After "Import", when the package also changes where your text goes or what may run without asking

1. **Notice** Nothing in this list is applied unless you tick it
2. **Each setting** Shown as before → after, unticked. Here: a new server address (and model name) for the text model
3. **Saved key removed** A new server takes the key saved for the old one away, so it is never sent to the new server; enter a key for the new one afterwards
4. **Apply ticked / Keep mine** Apply ticked applies only the ticked settings. Keep mine (also Esc) applies none of them; the rest of the package is applied either way

1. **Click "Import..." and pick the file**A `.sykipack`; an older settings JSON file works too
2. **Check the contents**Items marked "will overwrite" replace what you have; if the package's API key fields are empty, your current keys are kept
3. **Tick what to import**Untick agent definitions and skills from anyone you do not trust
4. **Click "Import"**Settings apply at once (some need a restart); agent definitions and skills are used from the next agent run
5. **If "Needs your OK" appears, choose**A model server address, the switch that asks before an agent runs a command (when the package turns it off), Cloudflare Mobile Bridge and the hot folder are never applied silently. Tick what you accept and click "Apply ticked", or click "Keep mine"

Included

- **Settings:** General, AI Models, Agent & Quick Actions, Shortcuts, Sync, Other (chosen per section; the Auto selector settings are part of Agent & Quick Actions)
- **Agent definitions:** the app-wide and the project `agents.yaml`
