- **Skills:** those in the current project's `skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.gemini/skills` and `.codex/skills`

Not included

- **API keys:** only when you tick "Include API keys"
- **`.env` files:** the project's `.env` is never packaged
- **Global skills:** skills in your home folder cannot be chosen
- **Your notes:** a package holds only settings, agent definitions and skills
- **Agent confirmations:** your Run answers for agents that act without asking stay on this PC; the other PC asks again

Limits and details (secrets, backups, size limits, what "project" means)

**API keys and other secrets**

- With "Include API keys" off, the value of every setting whose name contains `apikey`, `api_key`, `api-key`, `token`, `secret`, `password` or `passwd` is emptied. A Git remote URL loses its `user:password@` part, and an address that carries a key in its query (`https://host/v1?key=...`) keeps the name but loses the value (`?key=`).
- In agent definitions, values of the same kind under `env:` are emptied (comments and layout are kept). If that cannot be done safely, the file is included unchanged and a notice says it may still contain secrets; check before you share it.
- The number of emptied values is shown on the export result screen.

**After you import**

- Settings are merged into the running app and saved on the spot; theme, language, toolbar and shortcuts switch at once. Sections you did not tick stay as they are.
- Settings that decide where your text goes or what may run unasked wait for your OK (see "Needs your OK" above): a model server address (its model name goes with it), the agent confirmation turned off, Cloudflare Mobile Bridge turned on or given another URL or token, the hot folder turned on or pointed at another folder. What you do not tick keeps its current value, and the result screen lists it. If you take a new server, the key saved for the old server is removed unless the package brings one; your other keys stay.
- A package does not record which system wrote it. If its shortcuts use the Command key (a package from a Mac), they are not applied on Windows: this PC keeps its own shortcuts and the result screen says so.
- If `config.json` cannot be written, the result screen and the status bar say so; the settings then apply only until you quit.
- Agent definitions and skills are written by syki::sok itself. A package cannot be imported by editing `config.json` by hand, because the running app owns that file.
- Targets: the app-wide agent definitions go to `%APPDATA%\syki-sok\agents.yaml` (macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/syki-sok/agents.yaml`), the project's to `<project>/.syki-sok/agents.yaml`, skills to `<project>/<folder>/<name>`. An agents file that does not parse is skipped with a reason.
- Whatever would be overwritten is first copied to `%APPDATA%\syki-sok\pack_backups\<date-time>\` (macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/syki-sok/pack_backups/`). That folder is outside the project, so skill folders stay clean. The result screen shows the location.
- An older settings JSON (one file with all settings) can be imported too; it covers settings only and may contain API keys. Choosing "JSON (settings only)" as the export format writes the same kind of file.
- Some settings take effect after you restart syki::sok; the result screen says so.

**What "project" means**

Starting from the folder of the open note (for an unsaved note: the opened folder, else the scraps folder), syki::sok walks up to the first folder that contains `.syki`, `.syki`, `agents.yaml`, `AGENTS.md`, `skills` or `.git`. The home folder is never treated as a project (so global skills are never carried away). If no project is found, project items show "needs a project" and cannot be ticked.

**Limits and safety**

- A package can be up to 50 MB and 3000 files; one file up to 10 MB, 100 MB in total after unpacking. Settings are limited to 2 MB and one agents file to 1 MB. A skill over the limits is left out of the export with a notice.
- Not packaged from skill folders: `.env` and `.env.*` files (templates such as `.env.example` are included), `.git`, `node_modules` and `__pycache__` folders, and symbolic links.
- Refused on import: unsafe paths (`..`, absolute paths, drive letters and the like), encrypted or damaged files, and packages from a newer version. Files not listed in the manifest are ignored.
- Skills are instructions an agent will follow, and agent definitions contain commands syki::sok will run. Import only from sources you trust.

---

## 04 Power User & Hackers Manual

**In one line:** syki::sok is a hackable tool for engineers. Over local TCP IPC (JSON-RPC 2.0) and CLI subcommands, you can control it fully from shell scripts and other editors.

### UNIX Terminal Pipe

**In one line:** Pipe a terminal's output into `| syki` and it is appended to the end of today's scrap. No setup needed

It reaches the running instance in milliseconds and is appended to the end of today's scrap (`scraps/YYYY-MM-DD.md`) with a timestamp and the command name. The window comes to the front automatically.

```
# Pipe a command's output straight into your notes
cat build.log | syki

# Record a curl result directly in your notes
curl -s https://api.github.com/zen | syki
```

The pipe input limit is fixed at 10 MB.

The text is read as UTF-8; text that is not UTF-8 is converted from the console's code page. On a Japanese Windows, the Shift_JIS output of `ping`, `ipconfig`, `dir` and similar commands arrives as readable Japanese, and so does a UTF-16 file shown with `type`.

**Windows PowerShell 5.1 shows `?` instead of Japanese.** Before the text reaches any program, Windows PowerShell 5.1 turns the output of a command into ASCII (its `$OutputEncoding` is `us-ascii`), so every Japanese character has already become `?` when syki::sok receives it and it cannot be restored. Run this once in that PowerShell window, then pipe as usual (put it in your profile, `notepad $PROFILE`, to make it permanent). Command Prompt and PowerShell 7 do not need it.

```
$OutputEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
ping 128.1.33.254 | syki
```

---

### JSON-RPC 2.0 API Specification

**In one line:** From any language, open a TCP socket to `127.0.0.1` and send newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 requests to control syki::sok.

1. **Read the connection details**Startup writes `ipc-session.json` (Windows: `%APPDATA%\syki-sok\`, macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/syki-sok/`). It holds `{pid, port, token, started_at}`
2. **Open the socket**Port 49152 is preferred, but if it is busy a random free port is used instead. Always read the port from this file
3. **Send requests**Send newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 requests
4. **Send the token**Put the `token` from that file in an `"auth"` field of every request. It is **required for every method except** `buffer.get`, `buffer.get_selection` and `tab.list`; without it (or with a wrong one) the call is refused with error `-32000` and nothing runs. The token changes every time syki::sok starts, so read the file again after a restart

**Breaking change for RPC clients that never sent the token.** Earlier versions (up to 1.9.0) ran every method when the `auth` field was left out. Now `buffer.set`, `buffer.append`, `buffer.replace`, `buffer.replace_selection`, `buffer.save`, `tab.switch`, `tab.new`, `tab.close`, `ui.activate`, `ui.toggle_split` and `ui.eval` (and any other method) need it. `syki buffer|tab|ui` already send it; an editor plugin or script that wrote to the port itself has to be updated. The one-line messages behind `cmd | syki` and `syki <file>` are a separate channel and are still not authenticated.

| Method | Params | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `buffer.get` | `{"tab_id": "..."}` | Retrieve the content, hash (first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256), generation index, and line count. Omit `tab_id` for the active tab; an id that names no tab is error `-32002` (no such tab), not an empty buffer. `buffer.set`, `buffer.append`, `buffer.replace`, `buffer.save` and `tab.close` take `tab_id` too. No token needed. |
| `buffer.set` | `{"content": "...", "tab_id": "...", "expected_hash": "...", "expected_generation": 12}` | Replace the whole buffer. Supports optimistic locking (a conflict error if `expected_hash` or `expected_generation` does not match the current value; the check and the write happen in one step) and, on a tab that is on screen, preserves the undo history. Pass `tab_id` to write that tab without switching to it (a tab that is not on screen has no undo history); without it the active tab of the primary pane is written. The answer has `tab_id`, `hash`, `previous_hash` (the hash just before the write) and `generation`. Token required. |
| `buffer.append` | `{"content": "\n- [ ] New Task", "tab_id": "..."}` | Append text to the end of the buffer. Pass `tab_id` to append to that tab without switching to it; without it the active tab of the primary pane is used. Token required. |
| `buffer.replace` | `{"start_line": 1, "start_col": 1, "end_line": 2, "end_col": 1, "content": "...", "tab_id": "...", "expected_hash": "..."}` | Replace only the given line and column range. Add `expected_hash` (or `expected_generation`) to detect conflicts. Pass `tab_id` to change that tab without switching to it; without it the active tab of the primary pane is used. Token required. |
| `buffer.get_selection` | `{"tab_id": "..."}` | Get the selected text and its start and end positions (UTF-16 offsets). If nothing is selected, it returns error `-32003` (no active selection). A tab that is not on screen has no selection, so naming another existing tab first brings it forward. No token needed. |
| `buffer.replace_selection` | `{"content": "...", "tab_id": "..."}` | Replace the selection (as a single undo step). The selection is read again to check it, so if it changed after you read it you get conflict error `-32001`, and if nothing is selected you get `-32003`. Token required. |
| `tab.list` | `{}` | List all open tabs and which one is active, with each tab's `encoding`, `eol`, `diskConflict`, `isScrap` and the `pane` it is shown in. No token needed. |
| `tab.switch` | `{"tab_id": "tab_123"}` | Switch focus to the given tab. An unknown id is error `-32002` and nothing changes. Token required. |
| `buffer.save` | `{"tab_id": "...", "path": "C:\\notes\\a.md", "encoding": "utf-8", "overwrite": false}` | Write a note to a file and bind the tab to it (autosave then keeps writing there). It never opens a dialog, never creates a folder and never replaces an existing file unless `overwrite` is true (the tab's own file needs no flag). `path` must be absolute, must end in `.md`, `.markdown` or `.txt`, and may not be a network (UNC) or device path, a Windows device name (`NUL`, `CON`...) or contain `:` after the drive letter; without `path` the tab's own file is written. `encoding` is `utf-8` (default) or `sjis`; a character Shift_JIS cannot hold is an error that lists where, and nothing is written. Answer: `{tab_id, path, bytes, hash, encoding, created}`. A refusal is `-32602` with a message that starts `not saved:` and names the rule; a note edited while it was being saved is `-32001` (the file holds the earlier text and the tab is not bound). Saving a tab to its own file is also `-32001` (`not saved: the file changed on disk since this note last read or saved it`) when another program changed that file after the tab last read or wrote it; `overwrite` replaces it anyway. A CRLF file keeps its line ending. Token required. |
| `tab.new` | `{"title": "...", "path": "C:\\notes\\a.md", "content": "...", "background": true}` | Open a tab and return `{id, title, path, existing}`. With `path` (absolute, an existing file) the file is read; a file that is already open is not opened twice (`existing` is true; its tab is refreshed with the file's text unless it holds unsaved changes). `path` and `content` cannot be given together. `background: true` adds the tab without selecting it. Token required. |
| `tab.close` | `{"tab_id": "tab_123", "if_saved": true}` | Close a tab; returns `{closed, reason?}` and never waits for a dialog. A tab without unsaved changes closes. One with unsaved changes shows the normal save prompt in the window and returns `closed: false, reason: "prompt"`. With `if_saved` the tab closes only if it has a file whose current content equals its text (line endings ignored), otherwise `reason: "unsaved"`. An unknown id is `-32002`. Token required. |
| `ui.toggle_split` | `{}` | Toggle 2-pane split mode. |
| `ui.activate` | `{}` | Bring window to the foreground. |
| `ui.eval` | `{"expression": "document.title"}` | Run an arbitrary JavaScript expression inside the app's WebView and return the result. |
| `buffer.find` | `{"pattern": "TODO", "regex": false, "case_sensitive": false, "whole_word": false, "limit": 200, "tab_id": "..."}` | Find text in a note. Literal text unless `regex` is true (Go RE2: no look-around or back-references); case-insensitive unless `case_sensitive`; `whole_word` matches whole words. At most `limit` matches (default 200, at most 5000, then `truncated` is true). Each match has UTF-16 `start` and `end` offsets and 1-based `line` and `col`. It changes nothing, but it reads the note, so the token is required. An empty or invalid pattern is `-32602`. |
| `buffer.replace_all` | `{"pattern": "...", "replace": "...", "regex": false, "case_sensitive": false, "whole_word": false, "expected_hash": "...", "tab_id": "..."}` | Replace every match in one write. The note is read, replaced and written with the hash that was read, so an edit made in between is `-32001` and nothing changes (your own `expected_hash` is checked too). With `regex` the replacement expands `$1` and `${name}`; otherwise it is literal. No match writes nothing (`replaced: 0`). The pattern rules are those of `buffer.find`. Token required. |
| `buffer.cursor` | `{"tab_id": "..."}` | The caret, even when nothing is selected (`buffer.get_selection` answers `-32003` then): UTF-16 offsets, 1-based `line` and `col`, `has_selection` and `length`. It selects, focuses and scrolls nothing. A tab that is not on screen keeps one stored position, so its range comes back collapsed (`start` equals `end`). Token required. |
| `buffer.select` | `{"start": 12, "end": 48, "scroll": true, "focus": false, "tab_id": "..."}` or `{"start_line": 2, "start_col": 1, "end_line": 2, "end_col": 9}` | Put the caret or a selection (leave out the end for a bare caret; offsets are clamped into the text). Offsets and line/column together are `-32602`. `scroll` (default true) brings it into view; `focus` (default false) gives the editor the keyboard, so leave it false while someone may be typing. A tab that is not on screen is not brought forward: the position is stored for when it is next shown, unless `focus` is true. Answers like `buffer.cursor`. Token required. |
| `ui.state` | `{}` | Returns `{active_tab_id, split, secondary_tab_id, preview, zen, fullscreen}`. `preview` is `off`, `full` (replaces the editor) or `side` (beside it); `split` is true for a side preview too. Token required. |
| `ui.set_view` | `{"preview": "off | full | side", "split": true, "zen": false}` | Change the view. Every key is optional and acts only when the state differs, through the same functions as the shortcuts, so the usual on-screen message may appear. The whole request is checked first: a bad value, or `preview: "full"` with `split: true` or `preview: "side"` with `split: false`, is `-32602` and changes nothing. Returns the new `ui.state`. Token required. |
| `ui.open_panel` | `{"name": "scraps_search", "query": "...", "mode": "meaning"}` | Show one of the app's own panels, as its shortcut would: `find`, `replace`, `scraps_search`, `settings`, `shortcuts`, `snippets`, `all_tabs`, `command_palette` or `about`. It runs nothing: no AI request, no command, no save. For `scraps_search` only, `mode` (`exact` or `meaning`) and `query` (at most 4000 characters) open the notes search in that mode with that text and start the search; **Deep search** stays yours to press. `mode: "meaning"` is `-32602` while Meaning search is off, and so is `query` or `mode` for any other panel. Token required. |
| `task.list` | `{}` | What the Task panel shows: `{running, recent}`, each task `{id, kind, label, status, started_at, finished_at?, error?, cancellable}` (times in epoch milliseconds). It never includes a task's prompt or output. Token required. |
| `task.cancel` | `{"id": "..."}` | Stop a running task, like the panel's cancel button. Returns `{cancelled, reason?}`; `reason` is `not_found`, `not_running` or `not_cancellable`. No method starts a task: that is yours to do. Token required. |
| `app.info` | `{}` | The same answer as `syki info`: version, folders, today's scrap path, hot folder, autosave, and `gui_running` (true here). No secret. Token required. |
| `config.get` | `{"key": "scraps.scrapDir"}` | The same answer as `syki config get`: every key, token and password is shown as `<set>` or `<unset>`. `key` is a dotted path (a number picks an array item); without it you get the whole file. An unknown key is `-32602`. Token required. |
| `scrap.path` | `{"date": "2026-09-24"}` | The path of that day's scrap file (default today), whether or not it exists: `{date, path, exists}`. A bad date is `-32602`. Token required. |
| `scrap.list` | `{"from": "2026-09-01", "to": "2026-09-30", "lines": true}` | The daily scrap files, newest first: `[{date, path, size, modified, lines?}]`. Token required. |
| `scrap.search` | `{"text": "deploy", "from": "...", "to": "...", "limit": 20, "ranked": false, "semantic": false, "kind": "note,log", "path": "...", "update": false, "cutoff": 0.85, "tag": "work,urgent"}` | The same function as `syki scrap search`, the experimental Meaning search included; the parameters are its flags. `tag` (a string `"a,b"` or a list, at most 8) keeps only entries that carry all of those tags (a tag written under a heading counts for the entries under it too). Each hit carries `rel`, `url`, `label` and `link` (`[label](url)`) for citing the note as a link. `-32602` for bad parameters and, with `semantic`, when Meaning search is off or a cloud host has not been allowed. The 5 s limit of a call applies: narrow it with `from` and `to` or `limit`. Token required. |
| `scrap.tags` | (none) | The tags written in the notes (a whole line such as `<!-- tags: work, urgent -->`), most notes first: `{tags: [{tag, files, entries}], files, undated}`. The same answer as `syki scrap tags`. `files` is how many notes were read and `undated` how many of them have no day in their name (a `from`/`to` range leaves those out). Token required. |
| `scrap.tag_edit` | `{"text": "...", "op": "add", "scope": "entry", "line": 12, "tags": "work, urgent", "return_text": false}` | Works out how the tags of a note change, from the text you send (the same rule as `syki scrap tag`): `op` is `add`, `remove` or `show`; `scope` is `note` (the default) or `entry`, which needs `line`. It reads and writes no file and touches no tab. The answer says which lines of your text are replaced by which (`start_line`, `end_line`, `new_lines`, `eol`), what was added, removed or left as it was (`added`, `removed`, `unchanged`), the tags that apply afterwards (`note_tags`, `entry_tags`), where the range is in the old text (`range_start`, `range_end`, which cover the entry and everything under its heading, and for an entry with a heading `heading` and `heading_line`), how many entries are under it (`descendants`), the tags it gets from the headings above (`inherited_tags`, farthest first), the places a tag could be attached to (`path`: the entry itself first, then each heading above it, nearest first, each `{line, level, heading, range_start, range_end, descendants, tags}`) and, when something was not done, `message_code` (`already`, `none_found`, `front_matter`, `front_matter_tag`, `on_note`, `on_entry`, `on_parent`, which also sets `parent_heading` and `parent_line`); `return_text` adds `text`, the whole new text. A tag written under a heading also applies to the smaller headings below it: to put a tag on a whole article give the `line` of its top heading, and to take away a tag an entry only gets from above, ask again with the `parent_line` that `on_parent` gave. For the whole note `path` is `[]` and `descendants` is 0; every line number is a line of the old text. `tags` is a string such as `"work, urgent"` or a list (at most 8, 64 characters each, none holding `<!--` or `-->`; required except for `show`), and `-32602` answers a bad `op`, `scope`, `line` or tag. `changed: false` with `already` or `none_found` is not an error. To tag the note that is open: `buffer.get`, then `scrap.tag_edit` with its `content` and `return_text: true`, then `buffer.set` with the new `text` and the `hash` from `buffer.get` as `expected_hash` (if the person typed in between it is `-32001` and nothing changes). There is deliberately no method that suggests tags with AI. Token required. |
| `scrap.open` | `{"date": "2026-09-24", "background": true}` | Open that day's scrap file in a tab (default today). The answer is that of `tab.new`. A day with no file is `-32002` (no such file). Token required. |
| `scrap.append` | `{"content": "...", "title": "...", "cwd": "...", "activate": false, "format": "text"}` (or `content_base64` in place of `content`) | What `cmd | syki` does, with a token: append `---`, `## [HH:MM:SS] <title>` and the text to **today's** scrap file, start the Git sync and tell the page. `content_base64` is raw bytes, decoded as the pipe decodes its input (a BOM, UTF-16, Shift_JIS). Give exactly one of the two, at most 10 MB; empty is `-32602`. `title` is one line of at most 200 characters (default `CLI Pipe`). `activate: true` fronts the window (default false, so you are not pulled away from what you are typing). `format` is `text` (the default: the text in a fence) or `markdown` (the text as it is, so links and lists are live). Answer: `{success, path, date, time, title, line, bytes}`. It writes your scrap file: say so. Token required. |
| `git.status` | `{}` | `{git_installed, git_version, scrap_dir, is_git, remote_url, branch, clean, sync_enabled}`. `remote_url` never carries a user name or a password. Token required. |
| `git.sync` | `{}` | Start commit, pull and push of the scraps folder in the background, as the automatic sync does after an edit, and return at once (`git.status` shows how it went). `{triggered: false}` when the sync is not switched on (Settings → Sync). It pushes your notes to your remote, so call it only when the user asked. Token required. |
| `filter.validate` | `{"command": "git status"}` | The verdict of the Command Bar's guard (the `reviewed` mode, as `syki jev verify --mode reviewed`): `{safe, warning, blocked, risk_level, reason}`. It runs nothing. Token required. |
| `filter.run` | `{"command": "sort", "input": "...", "confirm_warning": false, "timeout_ms": 5000}` | Run a shell command with `input` on its standard input, as the Command Bar does with the selection; no note is touched (read the text with `buffer.get_selection`, write the answer with `buffer.replace_selection`). The guard decides first: a blocked command is `-32602` and nothing runs; a command it warns about is `-32602` until `confirm_warning` is true, which a caller sends only when the person agreed. 5 s by default, 8 s at most (then `-32603`); each output stream is cut at 1 MB (`truncated`). Answer: `{stdout, stderr, exit_code, truncated, risk_level, duration_ms}`. It runs a program on your PC: only when asked. Token required. |
| `print.pdf` | `{"out": "C:\\notes\\a.pdf", "tab_id": "...", "paper": "a4", "landscape": false, "margin": "normal", "scale": 100, "pages": "1-3, 5", "header_footer": false, "overwrite": false}` | Save a note's preview as a PDF, the same file as **Save as PDF** in the print panel. **Windows only**: on a Mac it is `-32603` (`not available on this platform`). `out` must be an absolute path ending in `.pdf`, in a folder that exists (else `-32602`); a file that is already there is `-32001` unless `overwrite` is true. `paper` is `a4` (default), `a3`, `b5` or `letter`; `margin` is `normal` (20 mm, default) or `narrow` (10 mm); `scale` is 25 to 200 (default 100); `pages` is like `1-3, 5`; `header_footer` (default false) puts the file's name above and its folder and the page number below. An HTML page is `-32602`, an unknown tab `-32002`, and a print already in progress, or the print panel being open, `-32001`. Answer: `{path, bytes, pages, tab_id}` within 8 s (the connection's own limit is 10 s); a huge note is `-32603` (`timed out`) and the file may still appear. The window flickers for a moment. It writes a file you did not name: say so. Token required. |
| `deepsearch.plan` | `{"query": "...", "limit": 10}` | A dry run of Deep Search: it searches by meaning (by words when it cannot, and `notes` says why), cuts the excerpts out with the keys taken out, and says which notes (`limit` 10 by default, 30 at most), how many characters and tokens, and where they would go: `destination.local` is true for a model on this PC, otherwise `host` and whether you have allowed it (`consent_given`). It sends nothing, runs no model and keeps nothing. It takes no filter: it plans for all the notes, whatever the window's Filter is set to. With no Text LLM set up it answers `model_configured: false` at once. The 5 s limit of a call applies. Token required. |
| `lessons.list` | `{"agent": "claude"}` | The Lessons kept for agents (rules a person approved in the app after a run went wrong; each time that agent runs a task they are put in front of its instruction). With `agent` (a key or an alias): `{agent, path, exists, count, applied, skipped, disabled}`, where `count` is the rules in the file, `applied` how many the next run is given (the newest, at most 30 and 4,000 characters in all), `skipped` the older ones left out for that, and `disabled` is true for `lessons: false` in agents.yaml (then `applied` and `skipped` are 0). An agent with no file answers `exists: false`. Without `agent`: a list of those, one per file of the lessons folder (`[]` when there is none). The same answer as `syki lessons list`; agents.yaml is read the way the app reads it, and a name that is not in it is used as it is. Read-only: no method writes a rule, because an agent could then rewrite its own future instructions. Token required. |

Every method from `buffer.find` down needs the token. A call is limited to 5 seconds (`print.pdf`: 8 seconds), and writes to a note are done one at a time. `app.info`, `config.get`, `scrap.*`, `git.*`, `filter.*` and `lessons.list` do not need the page and answer while it is still starting; the methods that read or change a note, the caret or the view answer `-32603` until the page is ready. `app.info`, `config.get` and `scrap.path`, `scrap.list`, `scrap.search` and `scrap.tags` give the same answers as `syki info`, `config get` and `scrap`; `scrap.tag_edit` works out the same edit as `syki scrap tag` but writes no file; and `print.pdf` is the twin of `syki tab pdf`; `lessons.list` gives the answer of `syki lessons list`. No method starts an AI request, an agent or a task, and none runs a deep search: those are yours to start. No method writes a lesson either; see Lessons for why.

Caution: the reads and the pipe are open to every local program

The token protects the methods that change something, but it is not a sandbox: the server listens on `127.0.0.1` only, any program of yours that can read `ipc-session.json` can call every method, including `ui.eval`, which runs JavaScript inside the app, and `buffer.get`, `buffer.get_selection` and `tab.list` (which read your notes) work without a token. The one-line messages behind `cmd | syki` and `syki <file>` carry no token at all. Treat the port as open to every local program for reading.

---

### Headless CLI Commands

**In one line:** Control syki::sok from the command line: read and write notes, switch tabs, check a command's safety, read the text in an image, and look up your scraps and settings, all from shell scripts.

Needs a running syki::sok

- `buffer`: `get` (also `get --out <file>`), `set`, `append`, `replace`, `replace-selection`, `save`
- `tab`: `list`, `switch <id>`, `new`, `close <id>`, `pdf` (Windows only)
- `ui`: `activate`, `toggle-split`, `eval <expr>`

Runs standalone

- `jev` (such as `verify`)
- `agent` (`prune`, `install-skill`)
- `ocr` (`syki ocr <image>`)
- `info`: where syki::sok keeps things
- `scrap`: `path`, `list`, `search`, `tags`, `tag`, `index`
- `config get`: your settings, with every key and token hidden
- `lessons list`: the Lessons kept for each agent (read-only)

- When output is redirected or piped, it is JSON unless you pass `--text`. To save plain text, use `syki buffer get --text > note.md`.
- `syki --help` (or `-h`) prints every command and its flags, and also how to pipe text in and how to call the JSON-RPC port directly (session file, message format, methods, error codes). `syki help buffer` prints one command's, and `syki --version` prints the version. They write to standard output, exit with code 0 and never start or raise the window, so a script or an AI agent can run them first.
- **Windows scripts, agents and CI: use `syki-cli.exe`.** `syki.exe` is a windowed program, so PowerShell and cmd do not wait for it and can lose its exit code and output. From the release that contains `syki-cli.exe`, the zip holds it next to `syki.exe`: a console program that runs the same commands (write `syki-cli` where this page says `syki`), so the shell waits for it and gets the real exit code (`jev verify`: 0 safe, 1 blocked, 2 warning) and the output. It never starts the app: with no arguments, a file name or piped text it hands the request to the running syki::sok, or exits with 1 and `syki is not running`. `syki.exe` is still the one that starts syki::sok. macOS needs no second program: the `syki` command there already waits.
- `--json` works on every `buffer` subcommand.
- `syki buffer get --out note.md` writes the note to a file as UTF-8 (no byte order mark unless you add `--bom`) and prints only its path, size and hash. Use it instead of `>` or `| Set-Content` when the text is Japanese: Windows PowerShell 5.1 re-encodes piped text with the console code page and garbles it. The file is written by the command itself, replaced in one step, and its folder must already exist.
- `info`, `scrap`, `config` and `lessons` accept their flags before or after their words (`syki scrap search deploy --limit 5`). They read and change nothing, with two exceptions: `scrap index` writes the search index (outside the scraps folder), and `scrap tag add|remove` writes a note only when you pass `--write`. They work whether or not syki::sok is running.
- `--tab <id>` (an id from `tab list`) works with `buffer get`, `set`, `append`, `replace` and `save`: the write goes to that tab **without switching to it**, without moving your cursor or focus. An unknown id is an error (`no such tab`). `buffer get --selection` and `buffer replace-selection` work on the tab shown in the focused pane. Before this change `set`, `append` and `replace` ignored `--tab`.
- **The JSON-RPC port now needs the session token for every write.** `syki buffer|tab|ui` send it for you; a script or plugin that talks to the port itself must send the `token` from `ipc-session.json` as `auth` (see the JSON-RPC section above; this breaks clients that never did).

```
# 1. Print the current buffer (plain text in a terminal; JSON if redirected)
syki buffer get

# 2. Print it as JSON with metadata (hash, generation, length, line count, ...)
syki buffer get --json

# 3. Replace the buffer with text from the terminal stream
echo "# Updated note" | syki buffer set

# 4. Replace it only if it has not changed since you read it (optimistic lock)
echo "Safe update" | syki buffer set --expected-hash a1b2c3d4e5f60718

# 5. Append to the end of the buffer
echo "- [ ] New task" | syki buffer append

# 6. Replace one range (line:column, both 1-based)
echo "replacement" | syki buffer replace --start 2:1 --end 2:10

# 7. Print only the current selection; exits 1 with "no active selection" on stderr if none
syki buffer get --selection
syki buffer get --selection --json
#   -> {"text": "...", "start": 12, "end": 48}
syki buffer get --selection --tab tab_2

# 8. Replace the selection with piped text, as one undo step
#    (refuses with a conflict error if the selection changed since it was read)
cat formatted.txt | syki buffer replace-selection

# 9. Check a shell command against the AST guardrail (exit code 0 = safe)
syki jev verify "git status && npm test"
# [SAFE] Command passed AST validation: git status && npm test

# 10. A blocked command exits with code 1; --json prints the verdict as JSON
syki jev verify --json "rm -rf /"
# {
#   "isSafe": false,
#   "reason": "破壊的コマンド \"rm\" は安全基準により実行を拒否されました (Destructive command blocked)",
#   "command": "rm -rf /",
#   "rule": "destructive",
#   "subject": "rm",
#   "level": "block"
# }

# 11. Choose how strictly the guard judges: strict (default, for one-click paths
#     nobody reviews), reviewed (a person confirms before running), or unattended (hooks)
syki jev verify --mode strict "sudo rm -rf /"
# -> blocked (exit code 1), in every mode
syki jev verify --mode reviewed "git status"
# -> safe (exit code 0)

# 12. Prune a Markdown file down to what is relevant to a query
syki agent prune --query "login bug" --file notes.md

# 13. Read the text in an image and add it to today's scrap (no running syki::sok needed)
syki ocr photo.png
# OCR text appended to C:\Users\you\Documents\syki-sok\scraps\2026-09-24.md
syki ocr --json photo.png
#   -> {"appended": true, "path": "...", "text": "..."}

# 14. Write the note to a file as UTF-8 (safe for Japanese text); prints only where it went
syki buffer get --out note.md
#   -> Wrote 1234 bytes to C:\work\note.md (hash 3f2a9c1d5b7e0a44)
syki buffer get --selection --out selection.md --json
#   -> {"path": "...", "bytes": 84, "hash": "..."}

# 15. Where does syki::sok keep things? (folders, today's scrap file, whether the app is running)
syki info
syki info --json
#   -> {"version": "2.0.9", "config_dir": "...", "scrap_dir": "...", "today_scrap_path": "...",
#       "today_scrap_exists": true, "inbox_dir": "...", "inbox_enabled": false, "autosave": true,
#       "gui_running": false}

# 16. Find scraps without the app: the path of a day's file, the list, and a search
syki scrap path --date 2026-09-24
syki scrap list --from 2026-09-01 --to 2026-09-30
syki scrap search deploy --from 2026-09-01 --limit 20
#   -> each hit: file, date, line, text, and the nearest heading above it (with its line number)
syki scrap search deploy --tag work,urgent            # only entries that have both tags (see Filter by Period and Tags)
syki scrap tags                                       # the tags in use, with how many notes and entries carry each

# 17. Look at your settings without exposing any key (safe to hand to an AI agent)
syki config get
syki config get scraps.scrapDir --text
syki config get text.apiKey
#   -> "<set>"  (or "<unset>" when empty; the key itself is never printed)

# 18. What can I run? Prints and exits; never starts or raises the window
syki --help
syki help buffer      # one command (also: syki buffer --help)
syki help rpc         # the JSON-RPC port: session file, wire format, methods, error codes
syki help pipe        # piping text in
syki --version

# 19. Install the agent skill that is built into the program (no repository or zip needed)
syki agent install-skill                # Claude Code: ~/.claude/skills/syki
syki agent install-skill --codex        # Codex ($CODEX_HOME/skills; the path is not verified)
syki agent install-skill --dir ~/agent-skills   # <folder>/syki
#   -> Installed the syki skill: C:\Users\you\.claude\skills\syki
#      (run it again later: "already up to date", an unedited older copy is updated, an edited folder is left alone)

# 20. Work on a tab that is not on screen, save it to a file, and close it (nothing on screen moves)
syki tab list --json                                  # the ids of the open tabs
id=$(syki tab new --background --text)                # a new scratch tab; prints its id
echo "# Draft" | syki buffer set --tab "$id"          # write that tab in place
syki buffer save --tab "$id" --as ./draft.md          # write it to a file (no dialog; refuses to replace an existing file)
syki tab close "$id" --if-saved                       # closes only if the tab equals its file; exit code 1 otherwise

# 21. Search your scraps by words in any order, or by meaning (experimental, see Meaning Search)
syki scrap search --ranked 納期 図面                   # notes that hold both words, best first
syki scrap search --semantic "the idea about sustainable building materials"
syki scrap search --semantic --update --kind note --limit 5 --cutoff 0 "using bamboo as a building material"

# 22. Check, preview and build the index that Meaning search needs
syki scrap index --status                             # settings and index state; calls no model
syki scrap index --dry-run                            # counts what would be embedded; writes nothing
syki scrap index                                      # build or update it
syki scrap index --rebuild                            # make it again (after the model changed)

# 23. Save a note as a PDF with the running app (Windows only; never replaces a PDF without --overwrite)
syki tab pdf notes.md -o notes.pdf
syki tab pdf notes.md                                 # -> notes.pdf next to the note
syki tab pdf --paper a3 --landscape --margin narrow --pages 1-3,5 --header-footer -o active-tab.pdf
#   -> Wrote <path> (N page(s), M bytes)

# 24. Add or remove a tag in a note file (see Add and Remove Tags). It prints the NEW text and changes nothing, unless you add --write
syki scrap tag show note.md                           # the tags of the whole note (add --line 12 for the entry that holds line 12, and what it gets from the headings above)
syki scrap tag add "work, urgent" note.md             # the whole note: prints the new text on standard output
syki scrap tag add booking note.md --line 12 --write  # the entry that holds line 12 and everything under its heading, written into the file
syki scrap tag remove urgent note.md --write
cat note.md | syki scrap tag add work                 # without a file the text comes from standard input

# 25. See the rules kept for agents after failed runs ("lessons", see the Lessons section). Read-only: the app saves them, after you approve; no command does
syki lessons list                                     # one entry per agent that has a lessons file
syki lessons list --agent claude --json               # {"agent", "path", "exists", "count", "applied", "skipped", "disabled"}
syki lessons list --agent cc --text                   # an alias works: "claude-code: 3 rules, 3 applied  <path>"
```

Limits and details (`jev verify` exit codes and modes)

- `jev verify [--mode strict|reviewed|unattended] <cmd>` runs the same deterministic, always-on AST analysis that the GUI's run gate uses. It runs entirely locally, and nothing leaves your machine.
- **Exit codes:** `0` safe, `1` blocked, `2` warning (not known to be destructive, but the guard cannot vouch for it).
- **Modes:** The mode does not change the rules, only how seriously a finding is weighed, because who is watching differs. `strict` (the default) is for one-click paths where nobody reviews the command before it runs, `reviewed` assumes a person confirms before running, and `unattended` is for hooks.
- A command such as `sudo rm -rf /` is reported as blocked in every mode.
- `ocr [--json] <image>` reads the Image analysis (OCR) settings and the scraps folder from `config.json` and appends the recognized text to today's scrap. In a terminal it prints the note's path, or `(no text recognized)` when there was no text (nothing is added then). With `--json`, or when the output is redirected or piped, it prints JSON with `text`, `appended` and, when something was added, `path`. Put `--json` before the file name. It works on Windows and macOS (cloud OCR only on macOS) and is what the Explorer Send To entry runs. See Send To menu and the ocr command.

Limits and details (`buffer save`, `tab new`, `tab close`)

- `buffer save [--tab <id>] [--as <file>] [--encoding utf-8|sjis] [--overwrite]` writes the note to a file and binds the tab to it, so autosave keeps writing there. It **never opens a dialog**, **never creates a folder** and **never replaces an existing file unless you pass `--overwrite`**; saving a tab to the file it is already bound to needs no flag. Without `--as` the tab's own file is written (a tab that was never saved: `tab has no file: give --as <path>`). `--as` is taken from the folder you run the command in.
- Only `.md`, `.markdown` and `.txt` files. Refused, with the rule named in the error: a path that is not absolute, a network path (`\\host\share` or `//host/share`), a Windows device name (`CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`-`COM9`, `LPT1`-`LPT9`), a `:` after the drive letter, a folder, and a folder that does not exist.
- `--encoding sjis` (also `shift_jis`, `shift-jis`, `cp932`) writes Shift_JIS. Unlike the editor's own save, it never swaps a character it cannot represent for `?`: it stops with an error that gives the code point, line and column of the first few, and writes nothing. No byte order mark is written and line endings stay as they are in the editor (LF).
- The file is written to a temporary file and renamed into place, so it is never half written; an existing file keeps its permissions. If you type in the note while it is being saved, the file holds the text from before your edit, the tab is not bound to it, and the command says so (exit code 1): run it again.
- `tab new` prints the new tab's id (JSON when piped: `{id, title, path, existing}`; use `--text` for the bare id). `--path` opens a file (a file that is already open comes back as `existing` instead of a second tab); `--background` adds the tab without selecting it.
- `tab close <id>` exits with 0 only when the tab is closed and never waits for a dialog: a tab with unsaved changes shows your save prompt in the window and the command exits with 1 (`prompt`). `--if-saved` asks nothing: the tab closes only when it is bound to a file whose content equals the tab's text, otherwise exit code 1 (`unsaved`).

Limits and details (`buffer get --out`, `info`, `scrap`, `config get`)

- `buffer get --out <file>`: the path is taken from the folder you run the command in, a folder is refused, missing folders are not created, and an existing file is replaced. `--selection` writes only the selected text and `--tab` picks a tab. The JSON has `path`, `bytes` (the size written, byte order mark included), `hash` (the value `buffer set --expected-hash` expects; for a selection, the hash of that text) and, for a whole note, `generation`.
- `info` prints `version`, `config_dir`, `config_file`, `scrap_dir`, `today_scrap_path` (not created), `today_scrap_exists`, `inbox_dir`, `inbox_enabled`, `autosave` and `gui_running` (a live app is listening on the port in the session file). It never prints a key, a token or a remote URL.
- `scrap path [--date YYYY-MM-DD]` prints the bare path even when piped, so `$(syki scrap path)` works. `scrap list [--from D] [--to D] [--lines]` lists the `YYYY-MM-DD.md` files of the scraps folder, newest first (JSON: an array of `date`, `path`, `size`, `modified`, and `lines` with `--lines`). `scrap search <text> [--from D] [--to D] [--limit N] [--ranked] [--tag a,b]` is a case-insensitive search of every `.md` file under the folder: the notes with a day in their name newest first, then any other file, stopping after `--limit` hits (default 100). With `--ranked` it finds **notes** (an entry between two `---` rules or headings) that hold the **words** of the text, on any lines and in any order, best first (`納期 図面` finds a note that mentions both); in Japanese a run of kanji, katakana or Latin letters is a word and the hiragana particles between them separate words. When no note holds every word, the notes that hold at least half of them are listed (`partial`). One hit per note, `--limit` counts notes; JSON adds `ranked` and, per match, `score` and `partial`. JSON: `{query, count, truncated, matches: [{file, date, line, text, heading, heading_line}]}`; `heading` is the nearest Markdown heading at or above the line, ignoring `#` lines inside code fences. With `--from` or `--to` only notes whose file name starts with a day inside the range are searched (`2026-09-27.md` and `2026-09-27_title.md` both count; a note with no day in its name is never inside a range). A bad date prints `Error: invalid date ...` and exits with 1; an empty result is not an error.
- `--tag a,b` keeps only what carries **all** of the tags (see Filter by Period and Tags for how a tag is written and what it covers). It can be repeated, takes at most 8 tags in all, works with every kind of search (`--ranked` and `--semantic` too), and a leading `#` and capitals do not matter. A line that matches is kept when the entry that holds it has the tags (counting the whole note's and those written under the headings above it); a ranked or Meaning hit, when its own entry does. A tag nobody uses gives no matches, not an error; more than 8 is an error with exit code 1. `scrap tags [--json|--text]` lists the tags in use, most notes first: JSON `{tags: [{tag, files, entries}], files, undated}`, where `files` counts the notes that carry a tag anywhere, `entries` the entries it applies to (a tag on a whole note counts all of its entries, and a tag under a heading counts the entries under that heading too), and the top-level `files` and `undated` are how many `.md` files were read and how many of them have no day in their name. It reads your notes only when you run it, writes nothing, and exits with 0 even when there is no tag (`"tags": []`).
- `scrap tag add|remove <tags> [<file>] [--line N] [--write] [--json]` and `scrap tag show [<file>] [--line N] [--json|--text]` put a tag into a note, take one out, or list the tags it has: the same rule as the Add and Remove Tags commands of the window. `<tags>` is one argument, a list such as `"work, urgent"` (at most 8; a leading `#` is dropped). `<file>` is a path taken from the folder you run the command in; without it the text is read from standard input. Without `--line` the tag is for the whole note; with `--line N` it is for the entry that holds line N, and, as in the window, for every entry under that entry's heading (a line above the first heading or rule, or in a note with neither, is the whole note after all). N may be any line of the section; to tag a whole pasted article give a line of its top heading. The line `<!-- tags: a, b -->` goes under the entry's heading, or on the first line of the note, or into the tag line that is already there.
- **It prints the new text and writes nothing, unless you add `--write`.** Without `--write` the new text goes to standard output, exactly (no extra line break), so `> out.md` and pipes work as with `sed`; the note on disk is not touched. `--write` replaces the file in place: the new text is written to a temporary file beside it and renamed over it, the file is read again just before, and nothing is written if it changed meanwhile (run the command again). It keeps the file's permissions, line endings and byte order mark, it never creates a file, and it refuses a file over 16 MB or one that is not valid UTF-8. It prints only a one-line summary on standard error. A note that is open in syki::sok with nothing unsaved simply shows the new text, but one with unsaved typing gets the red "!" (autosave pauses and you choose which version to keep), so for an open note use the window's commands, or `scrap.tag_edit` (below) and write the tab.
- **Nothing to do is not an error:** a tag that is already there (also through a whole-note tag or a heading above), or one to remove that is not there, prints the text as it was, says why on standard error and exits with 0. It exits with 1 when it cannot be done: the note starts with a YAML front matter (a tag for the whole note cannot go above it; tag an entry with `--line` or write `tags:` in the front matter yourself), the tag exists only in the front matter (syki::sok never writes one), or it belongs to the other range (a tag of the whole note asked for with `--line`, or an entry's tag without it), or the entry only gets it from a heading above (the message names that heading and its line: run the command again with that heading's `--line`), and for bad arguments. `--json` prints the edit instead of the text: `{changed, scope, start_line, end_line, new_lines, eol, line, added, removed, unchanged, note_tags, entry_tags, message_code, range_start, range_end, heading, heading_line, descendants, inherited_tags, path, parent_heading, parent_line}`, where `scope` is the range actually used, the lines `[start_line, end_line)` of the old text are replaced by `new_lines`, `range_start` and `range_end` cover the entry and everything under its heading, and `message_code` may now be `on_parent` (see `scrap.tag_edit` in JSON-RPC for the other new fields). `show` prints the tags of the whole note and, with `--line`, of the entry, and, when there are any, a line "tags it gets from the headings above: ..." (JSON when piped).
- `config get [key.path]` prints `config.json` with every string below a key named like `apiKey`, `token`, `secret` or `password` replaced by `<set>` or `<unset>`, and `user:password@` removed from URLs. `scraps.scrapDir` selects one value, `vision` one section; an unknown name prints `Error: no such key` and exits with 1. Add `--text` to print a single value bare.

Limits and details (`scrap search --semantic`, `scrap index`, `tab pdf`)

- `scrap search --semantic <text> [--from D] [--to D] [--limit N] [--tag a,b] [--kind note,log] [--path P] [--update] [--cutoff X]` is the Meaning search (experimental, off until `semantic` is enabled in `config.json`). It finds notes close in meaning to the text, best first, one hit per note, and cannot be combined with `--ranked`. `--kind` keeps notes or piped logs (AI results are not indexed), `--path` keeps files whose path inside the scraps folder, or whose name, matches (`sub/*.md`), and `--update` first brings the index up to date (at most 3 seconds).
- Without `--limit` it shows 10 notes (the word searches show 100). Notes scoring below `--cutoff` (default 0.85) of the best note's score are left out, and `notes` says how many; `--cutoff 0` keeps them. The cut is a share of the best score, not a fixed score: scores are not percentages and are comparable only within one `source`. Files that are not in the index yet are searched by their words, and when the index is empty or was made with another model, or the model cannot be reached, you get the ranked word search with `semantic: false` and a note that says why. A setup problem (the feature is off, a cloud host has not been allowed, no model name or key) is an error with exit code 1.
- The JSON adds `semantic`, `pending` (files not in the index), `left_out` and `notes`, and per match `kind`, `end_line`, `cosine`, `context` and `source` (`semantic`, or `words` for a file not indexed yet). In a terminal each hit shows `score: 0.71 (meaning)` or `(words)`. Every match of every kind of search also carries `rel` (its path inside the scraps folder), `url`, `label` and `link` (`[label](url)`, ready to paste) for citing a note as a link; a link opens the file, so cite the line next to it from `line`.
- `scrap index [--status] [--rebuild] [--dry-run] [--force] [--settle MIN] [--yes]` builds or updates the index. Only files whose size and time changed are read, and only text pieces never embedded before are sent to the model, so a run with nothing new costs nothing and an interrupted run goes on from where it stopped. `--status` shows the settings, the index and how many files are not in it, and calls no model. `--dry-run` counts what would be embedded and writes nothing. `--rebuild` makes the index again (needed after the model or the way notes are cut up changed; the old index is used until the new one is complete). `--force` reads every file again and `--settle MIN` leaves files changed less than MIN minutes ago for the next run.
- `scrap index` writes only the index: `index/<id>` in the settings folder, never inside the scraps folder, and it may be deleted at any time. A model that is not on this PC is used only for a host listed under `semantic.privacy.cloudConsent` (otherwise it exits with 1 before anything is sent), and a run that would send more than 1000 text pieces needs `--yes`. Do not add `--yes` for someone else: it sends their notes to that host.
- `tab pdf [<file>] [-o|--out <file.pdf>] [--tab <id>] [--paper a4|a3|b5|letter] [--landscape] [--margin normal|narrow] [--scale N] [--pages 1-3,5] [--header-footer] [--overwrite]` saves a note as a PDF, made by the **running** app from its preview, the same PDF as **Save as PDF** in the print panel. **Windows only**: on a Mac it answers an error. Which note: `<file>` (taken from the folder you run the command in; it is opened in a background tab for the print and closed again, and a file that was already open stays open), `--tab <id>`, or the active tab. `<file>` and `--tab` together are an error.
- `tab pdf`: `--out` is required unless you give a `<file>`; then the PDF goes next to it as `<name>.pdf`. A PDF that is already there is never replaced unless you add `--overwrite`. `--margin normal` is 20 mm and `narrow` 10 mm; `--header-footer` (off by default) puts the file's name above and its folder and the page number below. In a terminal it prints `Wrote <path> (N page(s), M bytes)`; piped, JSON `{path, bytes, pages, tab_id}`. The window flickers for a moment while the preview is shown. The command waits 10 seconds and the app 8, so a huge note is an error, though the file may still appear. A program older than this command answers `unknown tab action`; `syki help tab` shows what yours has. The JSON-RPC method behind it is `print.pdf`.

---

### Let an AI agent configure syki::sok

**In one line:** An AI agent such as Claude Code can set up API keys, models, agents.yaml and environment variables for you. Just paste one of the requests below. Agent CLI needed separately

**You**Quit syki::sok and back up the files

**Ask the agent**Hand over a request from below

**Edit the config files**Edit, then validate the syntax

**Restart syki::sok**You start it as usual

**Check each feature**Test each feature and report

**Which file, who edits it, and when it takes effect**

| File | Where | When it takes effect | Who edits it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `config.json`App settings (keys, models, shortcuts and more) | Windows: `%APPDATA%\syki-sok\`macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/syki-sok/` | When you restart syki::sok. It is read at startup, and the whole file is rewritten every time you save in the settings screen | The agent, **only while syki::sok is fully closed** |
| `agents.yaml`Agent, alias, notation and snippet definitions | Per project: `<scraps folder>/.syki-sok/agents.yaml`or the app's settings folder | On the next slot run. If it has a syntax error, syki::sok silently falls back to the defaults | The agent, or you (even while syki::sok is running) |
| `lessons/<agent>.md`Rules kept with the Lessons button | The app's settings folder, in a `lessons` folder next to `config.json` | On the next run of that agent | You, in the Lessons dialog or by hand. The agent only reads them (`syki lessons list`) and does not write them: they are put in front of an agent's instruction |
| Project `.env`For agent CLI keys | The project root (see Delegate: agents) | Every time a slot runs. It is the only env file read when an agent runs | The agent |
| Environment variables | The OS user environment variables | For processes started after you set them (see the fold-out below) | The agent (when you ask for it in the request) |

To move a working setup to another PC, do not ask the agent to copy files; use a settings package (Export and Import Settings) instead.

1. **Quit syki::sok completely and back up the files**On Windows, quit from the tray icon (closing with ✕ leaves it in the tray). On macOS, press Cmd+Q. The backup will contain API keys, so keep it inside the settings folder
2. **Give the agent a request from below**Tell it to read `skills/syki/SKILL.md` first. Install the skill with `syki agent install-skill` (newer than 1.8.0), or take it from the release zip (v1.7.1 or later) or GitHub, as described below
3. **The agent edits and validates**Ask it to check the JSON and YAML syntax too
4. **Start syki::sok**Start it as usual, from the Start menu, Finder or the tray
5. **The agent checks each feature**Ask it to report what it could and could not confirm

**Request 1: Set up Gemini in one go (image OCR, voice input, Mermaid image rendering)**

```
Please set up syki::sok for Gemini (image OCR, voice input, and Mermaid image rendering).
First read skills/syki/SKILL.md and skills/syki/references/setup-guide.md.
Before you edit config.json, ask me to quit syki::sok (tray → Quit) and make a backup. Then put the Gemini key I give you only in vision.apiKey (voice and image inherit it).
For voice, set voice.model to gemini-3.5-transcribe, apiStyle to auto, and languageCodes to ["ja-JP"] (replace it with your language, or leave it empty to auto-detect). For images, set image.model to gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image.
Also check the environment and prerequisites these features need (network, microphone permission, general.pasteImageOcr and so on), and set up anything that is missing.
If something needs to be installed or an OS privacy setting needs to change, show me the command and get my permission before you run it.
Never print or commit the key.
After the restart, check each feature with a checklist, and report what you could and could not confirm.
```

**Request 2: Add or change an agent, and put its API key in the project's .env**

```
Please add <agent name> to syki::sok's agents.yaml (the global one directly in the settings folder, or .syki-sok/agents.yaml in the scraps folder).
First read skills/syki/SKILL.md and skills/syki/references/setup-guide.md.
Make a backup, and keep every existing agent and notation (slot_profiles / recipes).
Check the flags with <command> --help, and do not add any flag that skips permission prompts.
Put that agent's API key in the .env at the project root (KEY=value format, UTF-8 without a BOM). Do not print the key.
If Git sync is enabled for the scraps folder, add .env to .gitignore first.
Validate the YAML. If you changed notations (slot_profiles / recipes), tell me that syki::sok must be restarted.
```

**Request 3: Check every feature's prerequisites and set the missing environment variables and settings**

```
Please check the prerequisites of each syki::sok feature, and set any missing environment variables and settings.
First read skills/syki/SKILL.md and skills/syki/references/setup-guide.md. Then, one feature at a time, check every feature in the table in section (e) of setup-guide.md, "Per-feature prerequisites and verification": whether what it needs (installs, keys, environment variables, settings) is in place.
Set whatever is missing in the right place: config.json after syki::sok is quit (backup required), agent definitions in agents.yaml, agent CLI keys in the project's .env, and everything else as OS environment variables.
syki::sok's own LLM keys go only in config.json (environment variables such as GEMINI_API_KEY are not read by syki::sok).
If something needs to be installed, or an OS privacy or firewall setting needs to change, show me the command and get my permission before you run it.
Never print or commit keys.
At the end, report each feature in a table as "confirmed / not confirmed / not checked".
```

Prerequisites per feature and how to check them (table)

The agent reads this table from section (e) of `skills/syki/references/setup-guide.md`. You can also use it to check by hand.

| Feature | What must exist | Config key / variable | How to check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Text LLM(Ctrl+L, Alt+C, presets) | Local: Ollama and `ollama pull qwen2.5:latest` (or "Install Gemma 4" in Settings → AI Models). Cloud: a Gemini or OpenAI-compatible key | `text.baseUrl`, `text.model`, `text.apiKey` (Ollama needs no key) | Local: `curl http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags` returns 200 and lists the model. In the app: select a sentence, press Ctrl + L, type "translate to English" and press Enter. The translation appears below the sentence |
| Ghost text | Same as above (a small model is recommended) | `autocomplete.*` | Type 2 or more characters and pause for 0.5 seconds: a dim suggestion appears. The Text prediction switch behind AI in the status bar is on, and Tab accepts it |
| Ollama auto start and stop | syki::sok starts Ollama when a request to `127.0.0.1:11434` fails on `/api/tags`. If you move text and autocomplete off `11434` and save the settings, it stops Ollama (this ends all of that user's Ollama processes) | None | `ollama list` (on some installs, running the `ollama` command alone starts the Ollama app) |
| Image OCR(Ctrl+V image, Mobile Drop photos) | A Gemini key, or a local vision model (`ollama pull qwen2.5-vl:latest`, and `vision.baseUrl` set to `http://localhost:11434`) | `vision.*`, `general.pasteImageOcr: true` | Copy only an image and press Ctrl + V. It becomes Markdown |
| Voice input | A Gemini key (`voice.apiKey`, else `vision.apiKey`), the model `gemini-3.5-transcribe`, and microphone permission | `voice.*` (no environment variable needed) | Ctrl + Shift + R shows the marker. Speak, then press it again or stay quiet for a while, and it becomes text |
| Microphone permission | WebView2 asks for permission at the first recording. On Windows, allow desktop apps in Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone. On macOS, allow it in System Settings → Microphone (macOS behavior is not yet verified) | None | If you see "Could not use the microphone", permission was denied or the OS blocks it. Do not delete `%LOCALAPPDATA%\syki-sok\webview` without the user's consent |
| Clipboard permission | The Ctrl + Shift + V fallback (only when Markdown conversion on Ctrl+V is switched off) and Mobile Drop's "Text from PC" read the async clipboard. WebView2 may ask the first time | None | Copy rich HTML and press Ctrl + V. It becomes Markdown and a toast appears |
| Mermaid to image | A Gemini key and a network connection | `image.apiKey` (else `vision.apiKey`, `text.apiKey`), `image.model`, `image.aspectRatio`, `image.resolution` | Put the caret in a ````mermaid` block and choose "Diagram: Generate Image with Gemini" in the command palette. You get an image link (save the note first) |
| Mermaid from text | Text LLM | `text.*` | Select text and choose "Diagram: Convert Selection to Mermaid" in the command palette |
| Command Bar (Ctrl+E) | The tools you pipe through must be on PATH (`jq`, `sort`, `tr`, `duckdb` and so on) | None | Select some lines and press Ctrl + E (if the badge says "AI CLI", press Tab), type `sort -u` and press Enter. The command runs in the app's working directory |
| Command Bar AI mode (Ctrl+E, then Tab) | Text LLM (or `cli.*`) | `cli.model` and others | Type "list files here" and press Enter: a command lands in the bar. Read it, then press Enter to run it |
| Slot agents | Install and log in to every CLI you use (`claude`, `codex`, `ollama`, `agy` and so on). The GUI app must be able to see PATH | Keys go in `<project root>/.env`, or in the CLI's own login | Settings → Agent shows whether the selected agent is available (a PATH lookup, cached for 30 seconds). Write `{{ say hello }}` and press Ctrl + Enter: the result lands. The error `エージェント起動失敗` (inserted in Japanese in both UI languages) means the command is not on the GUI's PATH |
| Auto selector(Ctrl+Enter) | For AI tasks: the text LLM (as above). For agent tasks: an installed agent CLI (see Slot agents). Command tasks need only the command itself on PATH | `autoSelector.enabled`, `autoSelector.agentConfirm` (both `true` by default; a config without them gets the defaults) | Write a line such as "Translate the checklist above into Japanese" and press Ctrl + Enter: the line becomes `[[ @llm ... ]]` and the answer lands below it, in a block. Settings → Agent shows the two boxes in the "Auto selector (Let it decide)" group |
| Quick Actions | Not needed for the local rules (an external engine is optional) | `action.*` | Press Ctrl + J in a note with text: up to 3 cards appear. An `sh` card runs in the app's working directory |
| Git sync | `git` on PATH. An **empty** remote repository. Credentials that work without prompts (a credential manager or an SSH key; prompts are disabled) | `scraps.scrapDir`, `scraps.gitSyncEnabled`, `scraps.gitRemoteUrl`, `scraps.gitRemoteBranch` | `git -C <scrapDir> remote -v`, `git -C <scrapDir> ls-remote --heads origin`. In the app: Settings → Sync, "Test Connection", then "Link / Init". Add `.env` to `.gitignore` first |
| Mobile Drop (same LAN) | Phone and PC on the same LAN (no AP isolation or VPN in the way). If asked, allow syki::sok through the Windows firewall on private networks | None | Ctrl + Shift + U shows a QR code and `http://<LAN IP>:<port>/?token=...`. Photos need `vision.*`, and voice needs `voice.*` |
| Mobile Drop (over the internet) | Install `cloudflared` yourself (Windows: `winget install --id Cloudflare.cloudflared -e`, macOS: `brew install cloudflared`). syki::sok looks for it when you press the button, so no restart is needed | None | `cloudflared --version`. Press the tunnel button in the dialog: an `https://...trycloudflare.com/?token=...` address appears within 15 seconds. Data passes through Cloudflare, so do it only when the user asks |
| Global summon key | None | `shortcuts.globalSummon` | Press it from another app. If it clashes with another app at startup, no error is shown. If you change it in the settings screen and the OS refuses, it reverts and a toast appears |
| Windows prerequisite | Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime (syki::sok cannot start without it) | None | Start the app |
| macOS prerequisite | macOS 10.15 or later. For a build without Apple notarization, the first launch needs System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway (macOS 15 or later) or right-click → Open (macOS 14 or earlier); `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "syki-sok.app"` works on any version | None | By design there is no tray. Use the Dock icon and the hotkey to bring the window back |

About environment variables (what is read and what is not)

- **Variables syki::sok itself reads:** `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` (else `JEV_API_KEY`), `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (CLI only), `JEV_MODEL`, `JEV_API_URL`, and `PATH` and similar.
- **Variables it does not read:** `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OLLAMA_HOST`. syki::sok's own LLM features read their keys and URLs only from `config.json`. These variables help only the external agent CLIs that read them.
- **GUI apps do not inherit them:** An app started from the Start menu or Finder does not inherit shell-profile variables. On macOS, syki::sok repairs only `PATH`. For other variables, use the project's `.env`.
- **Saving on Windows:** Save a user environment variable with `setx NAME "value"`, fully quit syki::sok from the tray, and start it again.
- **A good split:** agent keys in `<project root>/.env`, syki::sok's own keys in `config.json`, and OS environment variables only for additions to PATH and the Jev-related ones.

What the agent must never do

- Show, log, paste into chat or commit API keys, `config.json` (and its backups), `.env` or `session.json`. Keys are masked like "`set (...last 4 characters)`".
- Start a second syki::sok or force-kill the process. You quit it from the tray.
- Edit `config.json` while syki::sok is running. Do not delete a key to "reset" it; write an explicit default.
- Read settings with `syki ui eval`, or call `window.backend.*`.
- Point the scraps folder at a repository, your home folder or a drive root. Put `.env` in the scraps folder without git-ignoring it.
- Add a flag that skips permission prompts (such as `--dangerously-skip-permissions`) to an agent definition, or register a CLI it has not checked with `--help`.
- Start a Cloudflare tunnel, install `cloudflared`, change OS microphone, firewall or privacy settings, or run the `ollama` command without your request.
- Say "it works" without going through the checks. Anything it could not confirm should be reported as "not confirmed".

The folder to point the agent at is `skills/syki`. When you make a request, tell it to read `SKILL.md` first.

**Easiest: let syki::sok install the skill.** A program newer than 1.8.0 carries the skill inside it. Run `syki agent install-skill` and it copies the folder to `~/.claude/skills/syki` (Claude Code; `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is honored). It needs no repository, no zip and no running syki::sok, so it is also the way for a Homebrew install. `--codex` installs for Codex (into `$CODEX_HOME/skills`, else `~/.codex/skills`; that Codex reads skills from there is **not verified**, so use `--dir` if it does not), and `--dir <folder>` installs into any folder you name (the skill lands in `<folder>/syki`). It prints what it installed and where. Run it again after updating syki::sok: an unchanged skill prints "already up to date", an older copy you have not edited is replaced, and a folder you edited (or that this command did not write) is left alone, with the differing files listed, unless you add `--force`. Programs up to 1.8.0 do not have the command; use one of the ways below.

**Without the command, the skill is in the release zip.** From v1.7.1 the zip on the Releases page holds a `skills` folder next to the program (next to `syki.exe` on Windows, next to `syki-sok.app` on macOS), so use the `skills/syki` folder from it. Older zips, and installs made another way (for example Homebrew), do not have it: get the folder from GitHub instead. Either give the agent the address above, or download the whole repository (**Code → Download ZIP** on the GitHub page, or `git clone https://github.com/youshinh/syki-sok.git`) and use its `skills/syki` folder. An agent that can read web pages opens the four files in `references/` that `SKILL.md` links to by itself. To keep the skill always available, copy the folder (five Markdown files, about 340 KB) into your agent's skills folder, for example `~/.claude/skills/syki` for Claude Code.

---

### External Editor Recipes

**In one line:** From Neovim, PowerShell, tmux and more, you can send text to syki::sok with a one-line command.

**Neovim / Vim Send Command:**

```
" .vimrc / init.vim
command! SykiSend :w !syki
```

**PowerShell Clipboard Append:**

```
Get-Clipboard | syki buffer append
```

**Dump a tmux pane into your scraps:**

```
tmux capture-pane -p | syki
```

### Glossary: internal names and what they refer to

Release notes, configuration files, and CLI subcommands still carry the names these features were built under. You never need them for day-to-day use, but here is what they mean when you run into them.

| Term | Which feature | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Jev** | Quick Actions | An external judging model provided by TypeSafe AI — it is not built into syki::sok. It is used only when you enter an OpenRouter or TypeSafe API key under Settings → Agent → Suggestions (Quick Actions); it does not write text, it ranks syki::sok's built-in candidates. Otherwise syki::sok uses its built-in local rules. The name also survives as a CLI subcommand, as in `syki jev verify`, but `jev verify` (the AST check) runs entirely locally. |
| **Slot** | Delegate to an agent | The `{{ }}`-style notation in your note, and the mechanism that calls an agent from it. `slot_profiles` in the config file is where those notations are defined. |
| **Auto selector** | Delegate · Auto Selector | What Ctrl + Enter does with a line that is not already a slot. It decides, by fixed rules on your PC, whether the line is for the built-in AI, an agent or a command. It uses no network and no model, and it does not use Jev. It is not the quick selector, the popup that opens when you type `{{`. |
| **Result block** | Auto selector | The answer written below a task line, between two HTML comment lines (`<!-- syki:res id -->` and `<!-- /syki:res -->`). While the task runs, a one-line `syki:run` marker stands in for it. |
| **Snippet** | Auto selector | A ready-made task or command that you insert from the `{{` popup, from the command palette ("Insert task snippet") or with a short word and Tab. Your own snippets, under `snippets` in agents.yaml, join the built-in ones. |
| **Alias** | Delegate to an agent | An extra name for an agent, set with `aliases` in agents.yaml. `{{ @cc ... }}` calls claude-code because `cc` is one of its default aliases. |
| **Lesson** | Lessons | A short rule you kept from an agent run that went wrong (the **Lessons** button on a task card in the task panel). It is one line in `lessons/<agent>.md` in the settings folder, and from then on it is put in front of that agent's instruction. The command line and JSON-RPC (`lessons list`, `lessons.list`) only read them. |
| **System 1** | Quick Actions | The name for the fast inference mode that answers without deliberating — borrowed from the intuitive half of human thinking. It is why suggestions do not keep you waiting. |
| **3-Beam** | Quick Actions | The approach of offering up to three candidates at once rather than committing to one. Those are the three cards you see. |
| **MAP-Elites** | Quick Actions | The algorithm that keeps the three cards from resembling each other by picking candidates of different character, such as a Run card next to a Delegate card. Which kinds appear depends on what you are writing and on whether an external model is configured. |
| **AST guardrail** | Quick Actions / `syki jev verify` | Parses a shell command as syntax before running it and refuses it on detecting a destructive command, a write into a protected system directory, and similar patterns. It covers known dangerous patterns, not every possible risk. |
| **Ghost Diff** | Delegate to an agent | The soft amber band, with a 3 px amber line on its left edge, shown for the time you set over the rows a result was just merged into. Only those rows are marked. Esc undoes a slot's result while the band is showing and for one second after. |
| **Hover Peek** | Task panel | The latest output line from a running agent, shown so you can peek at its progress. |
| **Inbox** | Hot Folder | The internal name of the hot folder. It shows up as `inbox.enabled` and `inbox.dir` in the config file, and as "Open inbox folder" in the tray menu and the command palette. |
| **Meaning search** | Parallel Scrap Search | The **Meaning** side of the Exact | Meaning switch in the notes search: it finds a note by what it says, not by its words. It is experimental and off by default. It shows up as `semantic` in the config file and as `scrap search --semantic` on the command line, and the list it builds from your notes is called the index (`syki scrap index`). |
| **Deep search** | Parallel Scrap Search | The button of Meaning mode that sends excerpts of the notes it found to the Text LLM and writes an answer with numbered, linked sources into a new unsaved note. It always asks first. The answer note starts with the comment `<!-- syki:deepsearch -->`, which keeps such notes out of the index. `deepsearch.plan` is its dry run in JSON-RPC. |
| **Tag** | Parallel Scrap Search | A word you write into a note, on a line of its own, as an HTML comment (`<!-- tags: work, urgent -->`), so that a search can be narrowed to it. The preview and the print never show it. Above a note's first heading it tags the whole note; anywhere else it tags the entry it is in and every entry under that heading (the smaller headings that follow it). You can type the line, or let the palette commands **Add a tag to this entry**, **Add a tag to the whole note** and **Remove a tag** (or `scrap tag`) write and remove it; syki::sok never writes into a YAML front matter. The **Filter** button of the notes search, `scrap search --tag` and `scrap tags` use tags, and in JSON-RPC they are `scrap.tags`, `scrap.tag_edit` and the `tag` parameter of `scrap.search`. See Add and Remove Tags. |
| **Print panel** | Print or Save as PDF | The panel that the printer button of the preview opens on Windows: the printed pages on the left, the paper settings on the right, **Save as PDF** and **Print...** at the bottom. macOS shows its own print dialog instead. The same PDF is made without the panel by `syki tab pdf` and the JSON-RPC method `print.pdf`. |
